After watching for some time, Han Li gracefully entered the main hall and took his seat at the head, overtly observing the rough-looking middle-aged man, while internally he remained alert, ready to activate his dual protective divine abilities at a moment’s notice.
“Who are you, and what matters bring you to seek me out?”
Although he appeared young, being two hundred years old, it was quite normal for him to refer to himself as an elder in front of the middle-aged man.
Ignoring the youth of the Han Family Elder, the anxious middle-aged man hurriedly spoke, “Elder Han, my name is Zhang Xuan. I am the prime disciple of Old Master Qiuxuan, and I am here by my master’s orders, asking you to come with me as soon as possible.”
As he spoke, Zhang Xuan took out a token given to him by Qiu Xuan.
“`
Qiu Xuan?
Glancing at the token, Han Li’s brow furrowed slightly. He was all too familiar with the name, but why would Qiu Xuan urgently seek him out all of a sudden? Could there be some deceit involved?
When he cultivated at Tianxuan Mountain, Qiu Xuan was his fellow Sect Disciple, seven or eight years his junior. The two of them had a good relationship, promoted to the rank of Foreign Disciples together, and ventured out into the world side by side.
Lamentably, after Han Li failed to break through to the Pihai Realm and left the mountain in despair, Qiu Xuan had sent him back to Lingjun City with regret before returning to Tianxuan Mountain to continue his cultivation.
Only after learning from Han Li’s failure did Qiu Xuan prepare thoroughly before attempting to break through the Pihai Realm himself, achieving success in one go and raising his status significantly on Tianxuan Mountain.
During his recent return to Tianxuan Mountain, many old friends visited him, yet Qiu Xuan indeed hadn’t come. Han Li thought he might be out experiencing the world and didn’t give it much thought. Now it seemed that Qiu Xuan must be in some trouble. After all, the title “Old Master” was something only used in the Mortal World; how could Qiu Xuan dare claim such a title on Tianxuan Mountain?
Thoughtful, Han Li continued to inquire, “What does Brother Qiu Xuan want with me?”
The rugged middle-aged man glanced at the waiting Han Family descendants, appearing somewhat hesitant.
“Speak freely,” Han Li said indifferently.
With no other choice, the rugged middle-aged man finally said, “The master has suffered a grave injury and is not long for this world. Having heard of Old Master Han’s breakthrough to the Pihai Realm, he sent me to request your presence. The master said that the person he trusts most is you.”
Not long for this world?
Han Li was startled. What had his old friend gotten himself into to suffer such a grave injury?
Han Li had been closely observing the rugged middle-aged man’s expression and knew he wasn’t lying. Coupled with the information he provided, Han Li was quite convinced, albeit still hesitant.
Han Li gestured with his hand.
The waiting descendant immediately escorted the rugged man out to wait outside.
“Ah, what to do?” Han Li’s expression struggled with the decision.
His relationship with Qiu Xuan was one forged in life-and-death situations, lasting over a hundred years. Although they hadn’t been in touch for the past fifty years, their friendship remained unchanged.
Now that Qiu Xuan was gravely injured and near death, asking him to come was likely about entrusting his final affairs and ensuring his family’s welfare.
This was not a big problem for Han Li. His worry was whether there might be something more significant behind it all. It was out of character for Qiu Xuan to sustain such severe injuries without a reason.
Had the enemy who left him critically wounded died? If not, and still alive, they might be stronger than Qiu Xuan, potentially even a Gangyuan Realm expert, with a powerful Sect behind them…
This was the reason for Han Li’s hesitation.
He was accustomed to caution, having not engaged in combat for fifty years. Although he had achieved the advanced stages of the Pihai Realm, the eighth level, and possessed two Lower Grade Profound Rank martial arts, any action would expose his abilities, attracting unwanted trouble.
If the enemy was from the Pihai Realm, Han Li was confident he could vanquish them. But if they were from the Gangyuan Realm, he feared he could only ensure his own safety. Not only would he be unable to avenge his friend, but he would also draw the attention of a formidable foe.
Half a quarter-hour later, Han Li exited the great hall, his expression once again as placid as a still well. To the anxiously waiting rugged man, he said,
“Let’s go, take me to Brother Qiu Xuan.”
“That’s great!”
The rugged middle-aged man was overjoyed. He had finally heard the words he had been waiting for. Though he had only waited outside the grand hall for half a quarter-hour, it felt to him as long as years, filled with torment. He feared that if Old Master Han did not come, his master could not rest peacefully in death.
Soon, Han Li and Zhang Xuan left Lingjun City, heading toward the city where Qiu Xuan was located. Zhang Xuan, having a lower realm and unable to fly, to save time, Han Li carried him in flight. Fortunately, Han Li’s realm had advanced to the later stages of the eighth level of the Pihai Realm; otherwise, it would have been difficult.
There was no choice, for Qiu Xuan was his life-and-death friend. Now that he was dying, Han Li could not ignore it—had he not known, it would be another matter, but now that he did, his own conscience would not allow him to stay away.
Of course, Han Li was fully prepared to handle any situation, wearing a Top Grade Yellow Rank inner armor and carrying the Sun Chasing Bow on his back. With his cultivation at the later stages of the eighth level of the Pihai Realm and mastery of two complete protective divine arts, even an ordinary Gang Yuan Realm adversary could not kill him.
Should a real Gang Yuan Realm enemy appear, Han Li would not recklessly put himself forward. Compared to his friend, his own life was more important.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 - 10 Taking Care of Senior Brother’s Wife and Daughter_1
chapters.content:
10 Chapter 10 Taking Care of Senior Brother’s Wife and Daughter_1
Translator: 549690339
Leizhou, Fenglei Manor.
Han Li, accompanied by Zhang Xuan, finally arrived at Qiu Xuan’s location after twelve days; they even rested several times along the way, almost exhausting Han Li.
Fenglei Manor was even farther from Tianxuan Mountain, and given that Han Li maintained his Qi Sea at over fifty percent for safety, they took additional time.
“He hasn’t passed away yet, has he?”
Gazing at the city in front of him which was several times larger than Lingjun City, Han Li muttered to himself.
The city ahead was the city of Fenglei Manor, with a population of over ten million, including many more cultivators and naturally, more powerful ones.
On the way, Han Li had already asked Zhang Xuan about the situations in Fenglei City and the Qiu Family in detail.
In Fenglei City, there were over ten Gangyuan Realm cultivators who belonged to three major forces, and there were even more in the Pihai Realm—over a hundred, with Qiu Xuan being just one of them.
Twenty years ago, for some unknown reason, Qiu Xuan left Tianxuan Mountain to settle in Fenglei City, where he married and had children, establishing the Qiu Family. Zhang Xuan was the first disciple Qiu Xuan took over a decade ago; he was clearly trusted, or else he wouldn’t have been entrusted with the task of delivering the message.
A year ago, Qiu Xuan hurried back from the outside, haggard and seriously injured. Knowing that he didn’t have long to live, he started making arrangements for his affairs, with the most important being finding someone to entrust his wife and daughter to.
Originally, Qiu Xuan had someone else in mind, but three months prior, when he accidentally learned of Han Li’s return to Tianxuan Mountain and breakthrough to the Pihai Realm, he changed his mind and decided to entrust them to Han Li—his brother in arms who was naturally the most trustworthy.
Therefore, Qiu Xuan sent his first disciple to Lingjun City to deliver a message, and since Zhang Xuan was not highly cultivated, he could only ride an ordinary precious horse, and only managed to deliver the news to Han Li over a dozen days ago.
As Han Li thought about this, he entered the city with Zhang Xuan, heading to the Qiu Family.
This scene also caught the attention of the scheming, with Qiu Xuan on his deathbed, there were quite a few who had set their sights on his inheritance. The legacy of a mid-stage Pihai Realm powerhouse was substantial, and a widow and orphan couldn’t possibly guard it.
Qiu Family.
Han Li was led by Zhang Xuan all the way to Qiu Xuan’s bedroom, holding his breath along the way, ready to lash out at any moment.
Qiu Xuan would naturally not attack him, but he feared that Qiu Xuan had long since died and enemies used his name to lure him here.
Having survived in this world for nearly two hundred years, Han Li was acutely aware of the perils of the Cultivation Realm; he had to be on guard, or else a single misstep could lead to disaster.
Upon seeing Qiu Xuan, Han Li finally let go of his last sliver of vigilance. Qiu Xuan was in a dire state, lying on the bed, barely breathing, close to death at any moment.
However, just to wait for Han Li’s arrival, he had suppressed his injuries with his cultivation, clinging to life, refusing to leave.
“Master!”
“Disciple has returned late.”
Upon entering and seeing Qiu Xuan’s condition, Zhang Xuan suddenly knelt on the ground, tears streaming down, filled with self-reproach.
The disciples of Qiu Xuan, who had been guarding outside, all had their eyes redden upon hearing the words. After taking them as disciples, Qiu Xuan had devotedly taught and cared for them. Now that their master was dying, they were naturally in great distress.
Moreover, Qiu Xuan was their greatest support in Fenglei City; with Qiu Xuan’s death, they, being only at the Body Forging Realm and Rebirth Realm, would struggle to survive in the city.
“It’s good you’ve returned, cough cough~”
Qiu Xuan turned his head with difficulty, looking at the two people inside the room. His face flushed with feverish excitement as his consciousness suddenly became clear.
“Disciple, go out and stand guard; I need to speak with your martial uncle.”
“Understood.”
Zhang Xuan immediately withdrew, leaving only Han Li and Qiu Xuan in the room.
“Brother Qiu, it’s been a long time.”
Han Li walked to the bedside, looking at Qiu Xuan lying on the sickbed with a rather complex expression.
Qiu Xuan’s aptitude was somewhat better than his, and although he started learning later, his cultivation speed was faster. In the Cultivation Realm where strength is respected, Han Li had been calling him Senior Brother Qiu for a hundred years.
A few years after he left the mountain, he heard that Qiu Xuan had broken through to the Pihai Realm, but he never expected that their next meeting would be under such circumstances; truly, the unpredictability of life spares no one.
Now Qiu Xuan was merely experiencing a brief rally before his death and wouldn’t live much longer.
“Indeed, it has been fifty years.”
“Han Junior Brother has also ascended to the Pihai Realm, truly a cause for celebration, cough cough~”
Qiu Xuan, too, wore a complex expression, falling into reminiscence, and began to gasp for breath as he spoke.
“What exactly happened? With your strength, there can’t be many in Fenglei Manor who could inflict such a severe injury on you. Surely it wasn’t those from the Gangyuan Realm who made a move?”
Han Li’s brows furrowed tightly. Qiu Xuan was a Pihai Realm sixth-layer practitioner and a disciple from the Major Sect Tianxuan Mountain; even a late-stage Pihai Realm practitioner should be no match for him, and he should be able to escape from a powerful Pihai Realm Powerhouse unharmed, let alone sustain such grave injuries.
Qiu Xuan shook his head and said bitterly, “It wasn’t from the Gangyuan Realm, just two from the Pihai Realm who coveted a treasure I obtained from the outside world and ambushed me.”
“Though I managed to kill them using a secret technique, I also suffered extremely serious injuries that are beyond healing. Moreover, the secret technique considerably shortened my lifespan, and even if I could be cured, I would have only two or three years left to live.”
Han Li’s frown deepened as he initially thought there might still be a chance to save Qiu Xuan, but now it seemed hopeless. Qiu Xuan was enveloped in the aura of death, and the brief rallying only made him appear normal, but he had at most half an hour left to live.
“Sigh~”
Han Li exhaled a sigh, deeply affirmed in his conviction by Qiu Xuan’s fate—never to take risks without absolute certainty.
It was for a treasure that Qiu Xuan was attacked and killed, and although he managed to counterattack successfully, his end came just the same.
Fortunately, the assaulters were from the Pihai Realm, and Qiu Xuan had dealt with them; if they had been from the Gangyuan Realm, things would have been much trickier.
The room fell silent suddenly, with no one speaking.
After a while, Qiu Xuan spoke again, “Han Junior Brother, we share a bond forged in life and death, and you are the one I trust the most. Now that I am facing death, what I worry about the most are my wife and daughter. If possible, I hope the Junior Brother can look after them.”
“And my disciples too, it would be best if the Master could look after them a bit. If not, let them all leave the manor and city.”
“Everything I’ve saved is here. Regardless of whether the Junior Brother agrees or not, you must take it.”
With trembling hands, Qiu Xuan raised a hand to pass the Space Ring he was clutching to Han Li.
He was well aware that his inheritance, wife, and disciples would not be able to protect themselves; leaving it to them would only bring disaster. But entrusting them to Han Li, given his understanding of Han Li, he was sure that Han Li would take good care of them.
“Why make it so difficult, Senior Brother?”
Han Li sighed, and seeing Qiu Xuan’s pleading gaze, he reluctantly said, “Rest assured, Senior Brother, I will take care of your wife and daughter. Farewell.”
He actually didn’t want the Space Ring; the treasure that had brought about Qiu Xuan’s calamity was most likely inside it, which could bring trouble to Han Li. Trouble meant risk, and he did not wish to see that.
Seeing Han Li agree, a smile emerged on Qiu Xuan’s face, and his arm fell limply.
Han Li reached out to close Qiu Xuan’s eyes. He stared blankly at Qiu Xuan’s body when the eyes opened again, and in a weak breath, Qiu Xuan said:
“If my wife… chooses to follow in death, Junior Brother can… let her be, just take care of my… daughter…”
He did not finish his statement, nor could Qiu Xuan continue.
Han Li closed his mouth and eyes and waited a while longer before saying, “You may come in now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 11 - 11: One Pill Formula_1
chapters.content:
11 Chapter 11: One Pill Formula_1
Translator: 549690339
The doors swung open, and a procession of people filed in.
Aside from Zhang Xuan and a few other disciples, there were two other individuals, both of whom were beautiful women, who looked nearly identical, likely the wife and daughter of Qiu Xuan.
If Han Li had seen them elsewhere, he would have thought they were twin sisters, both in the flower of their youth, beautiful and delicate, one seeming vulnerable and endearing, the other pure and flawless.
Even by Han Li’s standards, the mother and daughter’s beauty scored over ninety points; they were certainly worth taking care of.
Han Li wasn’t the type to be unable to walk straight at the sight of a woman. He simply glanced at the two women and said, “Brother Qiu passed away peacefully and entrusted me with the care of both you, his wife and daughter, on his deathbed, and of course, these disciples are also within my care.”
“Condolences to you in your time of change.”
Having said his piece, Han Li stepped back, observing the actions of everyone, with his gaze primarily focused on the two women. He was particularly interested in knowing whether Qiu Xuan’s wife would choose to follow her husband in death.
If she chose to commit suicide, Han Li would not stop her. He would simply follow Qiu Xuan’s last wishes. If she didn’t wish to do so, Han Li would take on the reluctant duty of looking after the mother and daughter—cough cough—he most certainly didn’t have intentions of playing the villain Cao Cao.
Zhang Xuan and other disciples knelt behind her, not rising, their expressions filled with sorrow. Their master Qiu Xuan’s death had dealt them no small blow.
In front of the disciples were Qiu Xuan’s wife and daughter. At this moment, Qiu Xuan’s daughter, pale with grief and tears streaming down her face, knelt powerlessly on the ground, her lovely face marred by sorrow and sadness, her slightly open mouth uttering something.
By comparison, the bearing of Qiu Xuan’s wife left Han Li with a newfound respect. Despite her delicate widowhood and husband’s recent passing, her face was ashen and her eyes brimmed with tears, yet she did not seem overly aggrieved, as if a decision had long been made.
She leaned down to whisper to her daughter, murmuring words of comfort, then rose to her feet and addressed Han Li, “Your Excellency, I have a request that is difficult to voice… ”
Han Li nodded and said, “Go ahead.”
Han Li still held respect for the kind of courageous and loyal woman who dared to follow in her husband’s death.
He would not stop her from doing so because of her beauty, nor would he take advantage of her special status to sate his own desires by taking her as a concubine.
“My dear husband, I’m coming to join you.”
With Han Li’s assent, she smiled sadly, then flung herself headlong into a pillar, her head bursting and blood gushing as her body slid lifelessly down.
“No!!”
It was only then that her daughter, recovering from her overwhelming grief, cried out in agony, wanting to stop her, yet unable to do so.
She was stunned, kneeling in place, somewhat at a loss. Her mother had just said she would live on with her—why had things taken such a turn?
She looked at her father’s corpse, then at her mother’s, and swallowing hard, she gathered her resolve to follow her mother’s lead…
“Stop her quickly…” Zhang Xuan and the others exclaimed in horror. Before they could even call “junior sister,” they saw her being restrained.
Han Li’s figure flashed, and he was immediately beside her, his hand clasping her fair wrist to prevent her from seeking death.
“Let go of me!” Qiu Xuan’s daughter struggled incessantly.
Han Li shook his head and sighed, “Your father had anticipated that your mother would seek death, instructing me not to stop her. However, he did not say you should seek death as well.”
He guessed Qiu Xuan’s thoughts. Qiu Xuan did not wish to leave behind a dishonored name after his death. Entrusting his daughter to Han Li’s care meant that even if Han Li took her as a concubine, out of respect for him, she would be well-treated and able to survive well in this harsh world. Otherwise, how could a vulnerable woman survive alone?
“Father…”
Before she knew it, Qiu Yueyao’s face, innocent and tear-streaked, was a picture of pear blossoms bathed in rain, causing Han Li to feel an urge…
Han Li shook his head.
In the following days, Han Li took care of the Qiu Family’s affairs, burying Qiu Xuan and his wife together, casually killing off some of the little flies that had their eyes on the Qiu Family’s inheritance.
As Qiu Yueyao kept the vigil, Han Li opened the space ring Qiu Xuan had left for him and found a wealth of assets.
More than five thousand lower grade spirit stones, several Yellow Rank pills suitable for those in the Pihai Realm, more than a dozen mortal-level cultivation techniques and martial skills, and four Yellow Rank cultivation techniques and martial skills…
There was also a large pile of bottles and jars, which seemed to be elixirs for use by those below the Innate Realm, likely prepared for his several disciples.
Han Li meticulously took stock, setting aside the Spirit Stones, Yellow Rank Pills, and the Yellow Rank weapons used by Zhang Xuan, grouping the rest together.
“Eh? This is…”
Upon spotting this item, a glint flashed in Han Li’s eyes, and he immediately knew what it was—the treasure that had caused Zhang Xuan’s near-fatal injury.
“It’s actually a Pill Formula for improving cultivation talent!”
Han Li was shocked, not knowing how Zhang Xuan had acquired it or how the news had leaked out, attracting two assassins from the Pihai Realm.
Clutching the Pill Formula tightly in his right hand, Han Li’s expression wavered.
Compared to this Pill Formula, the other items in the Space Ring were worthless rubbish!
This was a Pill Formula for improving cultivation talent, how precious could that be? A priceless treasure!
This single Pill Formula, if its value were truly to be measured, could be worth half of the entire Daqian Empire.
The formula was named the Rebirth Pill, and although the materials required were quite rare, they could all be found. One Rebirth Pill could raise a person’s talent by one grade, up to a maximum of five grades.
Grade five talent, that was the potential of a Hollow Realm Master, a genius!
The Daqian Empire’s territory was vast, ruling over hundreds of billions of citizens, but how many Hollow Realm Masters were there?
Not even two hundred!
If a major sect got their hands on this Pill Formula and mass-produced the Rebirth Pills, they could create a production line of grade five talents. With vigorous cultivation, they could have the power to overturn the Daqian Empire within three hundred years.
Though the Daqian Empire was powerful, with several Grandmaster Wanxiang standing guard, and it was even rumored to have hidden True Martial Realm Kings known as Emperor Wu with lifespans of two thousand years.
However, it had many external worries. It was a sworn enemy of the northern Da Jing Empire; to the south, the demon sects’ top faction, the Yinyang Sect, had their eyes on it, constantly infiltrating, with the Hehuan Sect in Leizhou being one of its branches.
To the west lay the Buddhist Sect’s top faction, the Kurong Sect, a branch of the Buddha Domain, which had always wanted to spread its teachings within the Daqian Empire.
The previous Emperor Qian was extremely domineering, launching a campaign within the Daqian Empire to exterminate the Buddhist sects, nearly completely clearing them out of the empire. The few lucky survivors fled in panic to the Kurong Sect’s territory.
Should there be widespread internal strife within the Daqian Empire, Da Jing, the Yinyang Sect, and the Kurong Sect would all take advantage of the chaos to invade.
It could be said that this Pill Formula had the power to alter the major trends of the Xuan Domain. If the Daqian Empire obtained it and focused on development for several centuries, they could leap to become the foremost in the Xuan Domain.
The more precious the Pill Formula, the greater the risks that came with it!
Han Li’s hand holding the formula trembled as he wrestled within his mind.
“Zhang Xuan, oh Zhang Xuan, you’ve truly put me in a difficult position,” Han Li said with a wry smile, making his decision.
The risks of this Pill Formula were too great, so great that once exposed, Han Li would be completely incapable of bearing them.
All he could do was pray that only Zhang Xuan and those two from the Pihai Realm knew about it, and now that all three were dead, as long as he didn’t speak of it himself, no one else should know.
After all, Zhang Xuan obtained the Pill Formula a year ago; if anyone else knew, they would have made their move long before now and wouldn’t have left it in Zhang Xuan’s hands still.
As for where Zhang Xuan acquired the Pill Formula, Han Li did not want to know at all, even if that place might still contain other treasures.
Handing it over was out of the question—no matter the benefits it brought, Han Li wasn’t a fool.
Once handed over, they would silence him first, ensuring that no one else knew of the Pill Formula. Han Li wouldn’t even prepare to leak the slightest hint of information.
He had already decided to return to Lingjun City as soon as possible, to attend the grand birthday celebration, then to focus on developing securely for a decade or two. As long as no one came looking, he would be safe.
Then he could slowly collect the various precious medicinal ingredients listed in the formula, forge the Rebirth Pills, and improve the talents of himself, his concubines, and capable descendants.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 - 12 Welcoming Qiu Yueyao_1
chapters.content:
12 Chapter 12 Welcoming Qiu Yueyao_1
Translator: 549690339
After Qiu Yueyao finished her vigil, Han Li planned to take her and leave Fenglei City to return to Lingjun City.
Before leaving, Han Li asked Qiu Xuan’s disciples if they were willing to follow him back to Lingjun City, otherwise, he would send them to other counties within Fenglei Manor.
In the end, only Zhang Xuan was willing to follow Han Li back to Lingjun City; the others thought Lingjun City was too far and merely a county town; along with other reasons, they were unwilling to go.
Han Li casually settled the rest in a county town, gave them some cultivation resources, and then started the return journey with Qiu Yueyao and Zhang Xuan.
It was still Han Li who carried the two of them by flight, only the speed was much slower than on the way there. He wasn’t in a hurry to get back, as long as he arrived in time for the birthday celebration. If he didn’t make it in time, he could postpone it. Who else would dare say anything?
On the way back, Han Li kept part of his attention on flying, three parts on staying vigilant, and the rest on the Space Ring.
The principle behind the manufacturing of a Space Ring is very simple: the main material is a type of ore with spatial properties, which is then refined by an Artifact Refiner.
To refine a Space Ring, one needs at least a Profound Rank Artifact Refiner and to learn some corresponding spatial arrays for easy engraving. The larger the space, the stricter the requirements for refining.
Before this, Han Li didn’t have a Space Ring. Although they aren’t rare, they are quite expensive, and the main consumers are Cultivators of the Pihai Realm and above.
Previously, as an Innate Realm Cultivator, Han Li didn’t have many cultivation resources, so it didn’t make a difference whether he had a Space Ring or not.
“Qiu Xuan is actually not bad.”
Han Li thought to himself. Although it might bring him disaster, the probability was very small, and the benefits were tangible. Not to mention the Rebirth Pill Formula, the Space Ring and the resources within were a significant fortune that nearly doubled his wealth.
For the time being, Han Li had no plans to purchase a new Space Ring; a ten cubic zhang Space Ring was enough for his use for a while.
As soon as he saw the Pill Formula, Han Li’s heart heated up. Although he had no use for it himself, it solved a problem that had long troubled him.
Once his cultivation level was high enough, he could search for the appropriate materials to refine the Rebirth Pill, which he could then give his concubines to consume so they could reach higher realms and accompany him through the long years.
After calming down, Han Li was a bit confused. Why hadn’t Qiu Xuan offered this Pill Formula to the Sect at Tianxuan Mountain, instead choosing to wait for death and send someone to ask him to take care of his posthumous affairs in Fenglei City?
If handed over to the Sect, Tianxuan Mountain would have definitely given generous rewards, and Qiu Xuan’s injuries could have been easily healed, with the future possibility of advancing to the Hollow Realm Master.
What Han Li didn’t know was that Qiu Xuan indeed considered offering the Pill Formula to Tianxuan Mountain, but he was incapacitated.
He had offended an inner gate Elder of the Tianxuan Mountain, a true person of the God Refining Realm. To appease the anger and save his life, he voluntarily promised to leave Tianxuan Mountain and never return, nor would he allow his disciples to join the Sect. Only then did the Elder spare him.
The Pill Formula that could enhance Cultivation Talent was too precious; Qiu Xuan dared not tell anyone, fearing the news might leak.
If he informed his disciples to report to Tianxuan Mountain, there was a potential they could turn traitor and divulge the information to the major powers of Fenglei City. Even if the disciples remained loyal, arriving safely at Tianxuan Mountain and making the report, it was likely that the inner gate Elder, upon learning that his disciple had come, would first think to suppress the matter.
Even if the Elder didn’t kill the disciple, he might capture and interrogate them for information. If the Elder learned of the Pill Formula, there was a fear he would come to snatch it and eradicate any loose ends.
There were too many uncertainties, and under various reasons, Qiu Xuan didn’t dare take the risk. If his family was endangered, it would be too late for regrets.
He could only blame his own misfortune; after his breakthrough to the Pihai Realm, he had injured the beloved grandson of that inner gate Elder due to a dispute.
Three days before the grand birthday celebration, Han Li, bringing Qiu Yueyao and Zhang Xuan, returned to Lingjun City, weary from the journey.
He had corresponding arrangements for the two: Zhang Xuan would become a guard commander in the Han Family, eligible to receive abundant cultivation resources. If he performed well, Han Li might even share some tips with him.
As for Qiu Yueyao, after some consideration, she decided to marry Han Li as a concubine.
She did not dislike Han Li, in fact, she had a rather good impression of him. Han Li was handsome, had a high level of cultivation, treated her well, and was a close friend of her father.
Since she had followed Han Li to Lingjun City, and had no one to rely on in the Han Family, she simply decided to become Han Li’s concubine, thus directly turning from a guest into a hostess.
She had inherited Qiu Xuan’s cultivation talent, and even better, she possessed a seventh-rank cultivation talent with the hope of breaking through to the Gangyuan Realm, yet she had never joined any major Leizhou Sects.
Tianxuan Mountain was out of the question, as was the Hehuan Sect. The Sword Cleansing Pool had requirements for one’s talent in the Sword Dao, and the True Sun Sect only accepted male disciples.
Qiu Xuan’s original plan had been to wait for Qiu Yueyao to reach the age of twenty and break through to the True Qi Realm, then take her to join the sect of Fenglei Manor. Although it was far from matching major sects like Tianxuan Mountain, it was still a decent choice, but plans couldn’t keep up with changes.
Han Li had no objections to Qiu Yueyao’s request. Why wouldn’t he agree to a woman with a seventh-rank talent becoming his concubine? This way, he could also fulfill Qiu Xuan’s last wish.
Qiu Yueyao was not only nineteen years old, but her appearance was also stunningly beautiful, pure and impeccable, exquisitely charming, even slightly surpassing Li Mingmeng.
He had never taken a woman with a seventh-rank talent as a concubine before, which was a bit of a pity for her mother, who died so young. Had she still been alive, he could have fulfilled his filial duties.
After settling Qiu Yueyao and Zhang Xuan properly, Han Li returned to the back courtyard. He hadn’t seen his concubines for almost a month and missed them dearly; he certainly was not intending to perform any miracles through sheer willpower.
Soon, Han Li was living another round of blissful and joyful immortal days.
Three days later, Han Li’s two-hundredth birthday celebration took place as scheduled, and the whole of Lingjun City came alive, with festivities far grander than those of his past concubine acceptances.
All forces and wealthy merchants from Lingjun City and even Fenglei Manor either came in person or sent representatives. In any case, everyone presented a token of their goodwill.
There were also crowds of onlookers, causing the city to be overloaded with people, turning it into a sea of humanity, which in turn made Lingjun City even more prosperous.
On the day of the birthday celebration, Han Li received congratulations from his descendants and people from various walks of life, giving numerous formal speeches and exchanging business pleasantries.
A few days after the celebration, Han Li formally married Qiu Yueyao, making her his thirteenth concubine.
It wasn’t because he was particularly lustful; he wanted to use the occasion to wrap up affairs and then quietly observe and see if any forces were still investigating the whereabouts of the pill formula.
Of course, his attention to Qiu Yueyao would not be lacking; in fact, it would be even greater. The pomp of the wedding ceremony was much grander than before, after all, Qiu Xuan had left him a priceless pill formula.
That’s what he thought, but the outside world was abuzz with different rumors.
Having just celebrated his two-hundredth birthday, only a few days had passed, and the old ancestor of the Han Family had taken another concubine. Such a high frequency of concubine acceptances was astonishing.
The old ancestor of the Han Family was so enamored with the company of women that he would ultimately meet his demise through them.
Han Li was aware of these rumors but was too indifferent to care. After a billion years, all these people would have long since perished; who would remember these matters then?
At night, the Han Mansion was filled with great jubilation, brightly lit and decorated everywhere.
Han Li entered the bridal chamber and saw Qiu Yueyao sitting on the bed. Even though she was covered with a red bridal veil, she appeared somewhat nervous and uneasy.
Han Li smiled, walked over, and gently lifted her red bridal veil.
A face of pure, impeccable beauty and exquisite charm appeared before him, and Han Li immediately felt his heart stir.
The oil lamp went out at some point, and the quiet night was broken by the beautiful symphony of events unfolding.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 - 13 I’m at Nantian Gate_1
chapters.content:
13 Chapter 13 I’m at Nantian Gate_1
Translator: 549690339
About half a month later.
Han Li was leisurely lying in the garden basking in the sun, some concubines were giving him shoulder massages and beating his back, others were feeding him food and fruits, and yet others were dancing gracefully, revealing their charming dance moves.
All the concubines were cultivators, the weakest of them were in the Rebirth Realm, and many were in the True Qi Realm, which made their bodies more flexible and capable of performing more challenging moves.
“This really is the life of an immortal!”
Han Li exclaimed as he enjoyed the services of his numerous concubines during the day, and at night he would go to Qiu Yueyao to till the land, hoping to sow the seeds as soon as possible.
Qiu Yueyao was a cultivator with seventh-grade talent, and coupling with her held the hope of conceiving offspring with seventh-grade talent. By then, he would be able to receive rewards from the System again.
“Husband, I think I am with child,”
At that moment, Qiu Yueyao, dressed in a palace outfit and white skirt, walked over leisurely, her expression somewhat excited.
“Really? That’s great!”
Han Li had Qiu Yueyao come to his side and pressed his hand against her belly to feel for himself. He indeed discovered there was a new life within, just conceived a few days ago. Qiu Yueyao’s strength was not on par with his, so she was uncertain.
“Congratulations, sister,”
Liu Yuexin, Li Mingmeng, and the other concubines immediately offered their sincere congratulations.
As Han Li’s concubines, they also guessed some of Han Li’s thoughts and were happy to see a new addition to the Han Family.
Han Li nodded slightly, approving of the performance of these concubines.
There had never been any trouble in his backyard; the relationships between the concubines were quite good, and there was no bloody palace strife.
Of course, there were small factions; the concubines he took before reaching the Pihai Realm all followed Liu Yuexin’s lead, while those taken after reaching the Pihai Realm were led by Li Mingmeng. The two women got along very harmoniously and did not fight over anything.
Li Mingmeng, and even the newly joined Qiu Yueyao and other women, had no interest in managing the affairs of the Han Mansion, leaving it to Liu Yuexin, who was fair in her management. Li, Qiu, and the other women were happy to have more leisure time for cultivation.
After marrying Qiu Yueyao, Han Li kept a low profile and did not take any new concubines for two years.
During these two years, the number of Han Li’s offspring soared greatly, reaching 153. This was largely the result of the diligent efforts of his descendants, striving for Han Li’s rewards.
Because of Han Li’s reward system, the Han Family’s descendents were also considered to be blessed with many children, earning a vast amount of resources and wealth for each additional child born, which were raised by the Han Family. If the legal wife was unwilling to have more children, taking a concubine was the solution.
Of the forty-five new offspring, Han Li contributed to only nine. The concubines he had taken earlier had given birth to children, including two pairs of twins.
Li Mingmeng’s third child was born, and Qiu Yueyao’s first child was also born last year.
Of these forty-five offspring, twelve had cultivation talents, which was not a small proportion, mainly because the offspring of Han Li’s concubines all had talents. To Han Li’s slight disappointment, Qiu Yueyao’s first child only had eighth-grade talent.
While a bit let down, Han Li did not say anything as the next child might have seventh-grade talent, and it wasn’t something Qiu Yueyao could decide.
The surge in the number of descendants brought many rewards to Han Li.
He gained an increase of forty-five years in his cultivation, forty-five years were added to his lifespan, dozens of Yellow Rank Extreme Grade cultivation techniques, martial arts, and even secret techniques, along with dozens of Beauty Preserving Pills…
His own cultivation talent also improved greatly; roughly five more descendants with eighth-grade talent would allow him to advance to seventh-grade talent.
“`
Another reward was for having more than thirty descendants with talents, which currently numbered thirty-three, the reward is the same as when the count had broken through twenty.
Han Li spent twenty-nine years of cultivation to advance to the ninth peak of the Pihai Realm and did not claim the remaining thirty-six years of cultivation.
Once he officially reached the pinnacle of the Pihai Realm, the system provided a new prompt, just like one of his previous guesses, the cultivation years awarded by the system could directly enable him to breakthrough to the Gangyuan Realm.
The cost, however, was considerable—requiring one hundred years of cultivation.
This cultivation was not taken back by the system as a kickback. Instead, it assisted his breakthrough, taking one hundred years of cultivation as a catalyst to propel him into the Gangyuan Realm.
Breaking through from the ninth layer of the Pihai Realm to the Gangyuan Realm is quite difficult, and talent limitation is just one aspect; another aspect is the True Yuan.
Below the Gangyuan Realm, what’s utilized is True Qi, both acquired and innate True Qi are considered True Qi, but starting from the Gangyuan Realm, cultivators begin to use True Yuan.
To breakthrough to the Gangyuan Realm, one must liquefy True Qi into True Yuan, a process that is quite time-consuming.
Generally, a hundred strands of Innate True Qi are needed to condense into a single drop of True Yuan, and the process must be done with the help of a corresponding secret technique. Once half of the Innate True Qi in the Qi Sea has condensed into True Yuan, one will have advanced to the Gangyuan Realm. At the moment of advancement, the other half of the True Qi will automatically convert into True Yuan.
Even with a secret technique, cultivators of ordinary talent do not have enough time to reach the breakthrough threshold. But if they have a substantial quantity of Spirit Stones or even pill medicines that help condense True Yuan, they can hasten the progress.
Cultivators with good talent not only possess secret techniques but also gain access to many cultivation resources, making their breakthrough to the Gangyuan Realm relatively easier. Of course, the better their talent, the larger their Qi Sea, and a considerable amount of time is still required.
According to Han Li’s talent, after reaching the ninth layer of the Pihai Realm, he would still need to cultivate arduously for a hundred years to reach the breakthrough threshold of the Gangyuan Realm.
Although Han Li had such a long life-span, he would not foolishly choose to cultivate slowly on his own; to breakthrough while lying down, how delightful!
“Accumulate some more years, and it should be enough for the cultivation needed to breakthrough,” Han Li thought to himself.
Coming back to his senses, Han Li continued to engage in idle chat with his concubines, responding to nearly all their needs as long as it was reasonable, of course, these women also had a sense of measure and wouldn’t make excessive demands.
No one revealed the news of Han Li’s breakthrough to the peak of the Pihai Realm, not even his own women. Thus, the outside world still thought Han Li was a cultivator who had just broken through to the Pihai Realm, at most at the second layer of the Pihai Realm.
That was exactly what Han Li wanted, to mislead the outside world, and he absolutely could not let others know his true cultivation level.
Worrying about causing a sensation was one thing, but more importantly, Han Li was accustomed to being cautious to prevent potential problems before they arose.
The outside world thought he was a cultivator at the second layer of the Pihai Realm, but in fact, he was a peak Pihai Realm cultivator. If any shortsighted Pihai Realm cultivator dared to offend him, they could not expect to leave alive.
Even after advancing to the Gangyuan Realm in the future, Han Li would not immediately announce it but would find an opportunity to reveal mid-stage Pihai Realm cultivation, continuing to misdirect others.
In this way, if power sought after that Pill Formula, learning that he was merely a minor cultivator of the Pihai Realm, they might at most send a Gangyuan Realm Great Master to rob and silence him.
With Han Li’s Gangyuan Realm cultivation, even if he could not win, he would have time to maneuver and defend himself.
If possible, Han Li wished to accumulate more cultivation, so he could breakthrough on the battlefield, catching his enemies by surprise.
You think I’m on the first level, but in reality, I’m at Nantian Gate!
As time passed day by day, Han Li continued to stay inside Han Mansion, leading an ethereal life with his concubines.
Since no power came to inquire about the Pill Formula, Han Li felt he might be worrying unnecessarily, but he remained vigilant nonetheless.
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 14 - 14 Breakthrough, Gangyuan Realm_1
chapters.content:
14 Chapter 14 Breakthrough, Gangyuan Realm_1
Translator: 549690339
“`
Before long, another five years had passed.
Under the fertility encouragement policy of Han Li, the number of Han Family’s descendants grew at a rate visible to the naked eye.
In these five years, Han Li had been as stable as an old dog, never wandering out; even when descendants with eighth-grade aptitude reached the age of eight, he simply had someone deliver a letter of recommendation and escort them to Tianxuan Mountain.
During his last return to Tianxuan Mountain, Han Li had already formed good relationships with his fellow disciples, and his descendants, with a letter of recommendation, only needed to go through the process to successfully enter Tianxuan Mountain.
They all had eighth-grade aptitude, so why not recruit them? Giving Han Li some face wasn’t a bad move either.
Of course, if any descendants who entered Tianxuan Mountain didn’t strive to progress and hadn’t reached the Innate Realm by the age of fifty, they would be expelled from Tianxuan Mountain.
This was to free up disciple slots, reduce the consumption of cultivation resources, and facilitate the recruitment of disciples with more potential, thereby maintaining the vitality of the sect.
This rule was not unique to Tianxuan Mountain; almost all sects had this requirement, with only the standards differing.
As an inner sect cultivator, Han Li was entitled to an allocation of resources every year. He had been accumulating this for eight years now but had never gone to claim them.
Not needing them at the moment and with his family descendants not in urgent need, Han Li stayed within his gates to avoid unnecessary troubles, cocooned in Han Mansion, busying himself with procreation.
Even though he didn’t wander, concubines still needed to be taken; otherwise, how could he bless his offspring?
In five years, he took in concubines only twice, two on one occasion and three on another, totaling five, averaging one a year.
Under his diligent efforts, he achieved considerable success, and the number of his descendants saw a surge.
In five years, it increased by eighty-nine, and now Han Li had a total of two hundred and forty-two descendants, including sixteen new ones with cultivation talent. That was only four more than the previous count, mostly born to Han Li’s concubines.
Han Li wasn’t surprised by this. The descendants in Lingjun City were mostly without cultivation talent, and the wives and concubines they married were largely the same. The occasional birth of one with cultivation talent was already fortunate.
Each time Han Li took in a concubine, he chose female cultivators who had both beauty and talent. Although his descendants found it difficult to marry female cultivators with talent, marrying beautiful women was easy, resulting in the descendants of the Han Family being quite attractive.
A rumor even spread in Lingjun City recently, claiming that in twenty years, if the Han Family continued to marry and take concubines at this rate and with such standards, the beauties of Lingjun City would all be taken by the Han Family.
Common folks took it as a joke, creating topics for casual conversation after meals, but the smaller families and powers within Lingjun City were quite troubled.
It might not be possible to marry off all the beauties in Lingjun City in twenty years, but what about fifty years, or even a hundred?
Then, these smaller families and powers might really struggle to find beautiful women for their descendants to marry, which was a troubling thought for them, yet they had no solution.
As Lingjun City’s number one family with the old ancestor of the Han Family at its helm, when the beautiful women were to marry, most of them chose Han Family’s descendants.
The descendants of the Han Family were attractive, and as the wealthiest family in Lingjun City, marrying into it meant a life of comfort and a certain status, even helping their natal families rise in society. Why wouldn’t they choose it?
Moreover, the Han Family had a good family tradition; domestic abuse was almost non-existent, and the status of wives and concubines was not low. This was Han Li’s requirement, to treat every woman who married into the Han Family kindly, since after all, his descendants would come from them.
The descendants of the Han Family treated their wives and concubines very well, doing their utmost to pamper them. They wanted to gain the family’s procreation rewards, which depended on their spouses. If their spouses were unwilling, they would not dare to force them.
In the back garden.
Han Li ate a grape fed to him by Qiu Yueyao, kissed her, and smiled, “This is really sweet~”
Qiu Yueyao immediately offered another and said sweetly, “If it’s sweet, then Husband should eat another.”
“In my mouth, the sweet one is Yueyao, not the grape,” Han Li said with a shake of his head and a smile.
Qiu Yueyao’s face instantly flushed with a blush, appearing pitiable and moving, making one unable to resist kissing her, and that’s exactly what Han Li did.
Over the years, Qiu Yueyao had been well protected by him, long forgetting the sorrow of her parents’ death and maintaining her previous innocence and flawlessness.
Not just her, but the other concubines as well; with ample resources and under Han Li’s guidance, their cultivation advanced by leaps and bounds.
“`
Especially noteworthy was Qiu Yueyao, who with a Seventh Grade aptitude had only been married to Han Li for a mere seven years, yet her cultivation had already broken through from the ninth layer of the Rebirth Realm to the sixth layer of the Innate Realm, spanning nearly two Big Realms.
One reason was her excellent aptitude, the second was the massive supply of resources from Han Li: cultivation techniques, martial skills, medicinal pills, Spirit Stones, and so on. The third was the guidance from Han Li himself.
Han Li was, after all, a cultivator in the Gang Yuan Realm, and his cultivation had been painstakingly achieved, so naturally, he knew various cultivation experiences.
Indeed, Han Li was already a cultivator in the Gang Yuan Realm; it was just that no one else knew it yet.
The massive increase in the number of his descendants had boosted his lifespan by nearly two hundred years. Now his lifespan limit had been raised to nearly seven hundred years, nearly rivaling that of a Hollow Realm Master.
Sixteen descendants with cultivation talents, one of whom was a Seventh Grade descendant borne by Qiu Yueyao, and another an Eighth Grade aptitude descendant, had officially elevated Han Li’s aptitude to the Seventh Grade.
However, to progress to a Sixth Grade aptitude, Han Li still needed to efforts slowly. The effectiveness of his aptitude improvement was reduced to 4% for descendants with Eighth Grade aptitude, 2% for Ninth Grade, and still one-tenth for Seventh Grade aptitude descendants.
After the birth of the first Seventh Grade aptitude descendant, Han Li gained twenty years of cultivation and obtained the Profound Rank mid-grade cultivation technique, “Sacred Heart Scripture.”
When the number of descendants with aptitude broke through forty, Han Li gained twenty years of cultivation, one Seventh Grade Lifespan Extension Pill, and thirty years of alchemy experience.
There were other benefits such as eighty-nine years of cultivation, lifespan, a large collection of cultivation techniques and martial skills, a large number of Beauty Preserving Pills, and so on.
Along with the thirty-six years of cultivation he had previously accumulated, Han Li had a total of one hundred sixty-five years of cultivation. After using a hundred years to break through to the first level of the Gang Yuan Realm, he had sixty-five years of cultivation left unclaimed.
Once his aptitude reached the Seventh Grade, to cultivate to the peak of the nine layers of the Gang Yuan Realm would require more cultivation, at least one hundred and fifty years.
This might seem preposterous, but in reality, it was normal. A cultivator with a Seventh Grade aptitude would typically spend around one hundred and fifty years to reach the Gang Yuan Realm, and their lifespan limit would be four hundred years, giving them ample time to advance their cultivation.
The cultivation he had accrued was still insufficient, and Han Li was not keen on going out to fight and kill, as breaking through a few minor realms was of little use.
Currently, Han Li had switched his cultivation technique to the “Sacred Heart Scripture.” This Profound Rank mid-grade technique could be cultivated all the way to the peak of the nine layers of the Gang Yuan Realm.
Although Tianxuan Mountain possessed techniques for the Gang Yuan Realm and even higher realms, there was no reason for Han Li to obtain them.
The major sects imposed strict controls over the circulation of techniques, which were only provided for breakthroughs to the subsequent realms and reserved for those with aptitudes considered promising enough for higher realm advancements.
Previously, Han Li, with an Eighth Grade aptitude, had almost no chance of cultivating to the Gang Yuan Realm, so getting the subsequent techniques in advance was not permissible. They would only be provided if he managed to break through by chance.
The “Sacred Heart Scripture” had also become the best inheritance technique of the Han Family. There were over a hundred Yellow Rank Supreme Grade techniques, martial skills, secrets, and many more miscellaneous texts in the Han Mansion’s scripture library, all collected by Han Li. He would peruse them in his spare time to expand his knowledge.
He had also rewarded the hundreds of Beauty Preserving Pills he owned in a steady stream, a small portion to his newly accepted concubines and the majority to the wives and concubines of his descendants, leaving only about ten or twenty in his possession.
Besides cultivation, techniques, and lifespan, Han Li was most interested in those thirty years of alchemy experience.
This was the first time he had received such a reward.
The alchemy experience awarded by the System could be interpreted as alchemical cultivation proficiency, equivalent to thirty years of experience in learning alchemy, which could indeed save a great deal of Han Li’s time.
After all, the energy of a cultivator is limited; engaging in secondary professions such as alchemy and qi cultivation reduces the time available for primary cultivation.
Generally, only those unable to break through to higher realms would delve into alchemy and artifact refining—advancing one’s cultivation realm is of the utmost importance.
“Not bad, not bad at all.”
After absorbing the thirty years of alchemy experience, Han Li’s face showed pleasure.
He was now quite an experienced Alchemist, knowledgeable in many alchemy methods and having his unique understanding of alchemy. After examining a Pill Formula, he could refine it with just a bit of pondering.
If one had to assign him a level, Han Li could now be considered an Eight Grade Alchemist.
Alchemy and artifact refining were categorized into ten grades, from Tenth Grade to First Grade, where Tenth Grade entailed refining pills and weapons for the Innate Realm and below.
A Ninth Grade Alchemist could refine Innate Realm pills, while an Eighth Grade Alchemist could refine pills for the Pihai Realm. Similarly, a Seventh Grade Alchemist could produce Gang Yuan Realm Pills…

chapters.title: Chapter 15 - 15 I am an Alchemy Genius_1
chapters.content:
15 Chapter 15 I am an Alchemy Genius_1
Translator: 549690339
Han Mansion, Pill Refining Pavilion.
As the population of the Han Family had surged several times over, the original Han Mansion could no longer accommodate everyone. Han Li, with a grand gesture, commanded an expansion of the Han Mansion, extending its grounds by a large area, making it now cover more than five thousand acres.
The expanded Han Mansion instantly became more imposing and could accommodate many more people; only a small portion of the space was currently in use by the Han Family members.
Ordinary people and even family powers that originally lived around Han Mansion were forcibly relocated, and the Han Family gave them four times the compensation, which made them leave happily and without complaint.
This series of actions unexpectedly triggered a trend of real estate speculation in Lingjun City. Those with foresight knew that, given the growth trend of the Han Mansion’s population, it wouldn’t be many years before another expansion was necessary. By then, buildings around the New Han Manor would be within the demolition range and eligible for high compensation.
Consequently, the prices for housing and land around the Han Mansion soared immediately after the expansion, and as the population of the Han Mansion grew, the prices of the surrounding land continued to rise.
Many merchants, spotting a business opportunity, started to buy land at high prices in advance. Some who needed wealth immediately sold theirs, while many others chose to wait for relocation. Those merchants didn’t dare to do anything outrageous, for fear of angering the Han Family.
There was now an unwritten rule in Lingjun City: within ten miles of the Han Mansion, fighting and brawling were prohibited, lest they disturb the Han family’s elder ancestor playing in the back yard and suffer dire consequences—as had been learned from bloody lessons in the past.
The Pill Refining Pavilion was a sprawling pavilion specially constructed by Han Li, and an Artifact Refining Pavilion had also been built in preparation.
After the construction of the Pill Refining Pavilion was complete, Han Li moved in the materials required for the various pill formulas he had collected over the years and began his attempts at alchemy.
Han Li had collected dozens of Tenth Grade pill formulas, five Ninth Grade pill formulas, and one Eighth Grade pill formula. The higher the grade of the pill formula, the more precious it was. The collection of one Eighth Grade pill formula was indeed a pleasant surprise for Han Li.
As for the Rebirth Pill formula treasured by him, it was a Fourth Grade formula, which typically required a Fourth Grade alchemist to refine. However, this pill formula was an exception.
Its classification as Fourth Grade was mainly due to its immense value, as it could enhance a cultivator’s aptitude to Fifth Grade. According to the instructions, even a Sixth Grade alchemist could produce it.
After spending some time at the Pill Refining Pavilion, Han Li produced a large quantity of elixirs. He encountered no difficulty whatsoever with the Tenth Grade formulas, and only the Ninth Grade ones posed a slight challenge. The Eighth Grade formula required some serious effort, but the success rates for forming pills were high.
I didn’t realize I had such a talent for alchemy!
Han Li knew that this was the result of thirty years’ experience in alchemy, but why would he admit that? This was all because he was simply too much of a genius!
From then on, Han Li took to holing up in Han Mansion, finding himself a new activity—alchemy.
Every day, he would spend two hours refining pills. Spending any more time would yield not even a single drop more. This not only passed the time but also opened up a new avenue for wealth for the Han Family.
The Han Family’s business began to include the selling of elixirs, offering everything from the lowest grade, Tenth Grade pills, to Eighth Grade ones, selling them in large quantities to earn worldly wealth and spirit stones.
The population of the Han Family was growing so fast that cultivation resources were starting to become scarce. Every new child born in the family earned a significant reward, mainly worldly wealth, with a small portion consisting of spirit stones, elixirs, and so on.
Over the years, although the Han Family’s business had expanded across the entire Fengyang Manor, the speed at which they made money couldn’t keep up with the rate of consumption. Worldly wealth was quite plentiful, but spirit stones were scarce.
The spirit stones the Han Family business could earn were negligible, accounting for over ninety percent of worldly wealth, and without a spirit stone mine for extraction, Han Li’s numerous concubines were even using up spirit stones at an alarming rate.
Most of the Han Family’s cultivation resources, including spirit stones, consisted of Han Li’s savings, with only a small part earned from the family business. Han Li estimated that in about three more years, his savings would be completely depleted.
However, with the new prospect of selling elixirs, this financial hole could be filled.
Han Li had already ordered the Han Family to collect more Eighth Grade or higher pill formulas and was willing to take action personally if necessary.
Eighth Grade Elixirs couldn’t earn any Spirit Stones, while Ninth Grade Pills indeed could, but those in the Innate Realm were all paupers, meticulously calculating their Spirit Stones, mostly unwilling to squander them. Therefore, Han Li now wanted to penetrate the Pihai Realm market.
The current issue was that there was only one Eighth Grade Pill Formula for targeting the Pihai Realm, which allowed for a very small market share.
…
The expanded Han Mansion was overall magnificent and resplendent, with its pavilions, towers, and exquisite, elegant gardens resembling a picturesque scene.
The newly expanded backyard garden of the Han Mansion covered a large area, spreading over hundreds of acres, with a wide variety of flowers, plants, and trees. Inside the garden, peonies of all colors competed for splendor, sprouting delicate buds, in shades of red, purple, pink, and white, vividly intermixed and exuding a fragrant aroma that assailed the senses.
In the backyard garden, there were several ponds designed, filled with white lotus flowers and inhabited by golden carps.
Beyond the ponds, earth and stones were piled to form hills, with more than ten pavilions and towers constructed nearby. Numerous seating areas were provided along the banks, showcasing a variety of rare maps, ancient books, and precious antiques, which complemented the beautiful scenery.
At this moment, Han Li was dressed in a splendid robe of white jade, his long hair held back by a white jade crown, and a piece of purple jade hanging at his waist. His facial features were handsome and refined as if crafted by the heavens, and his demeanor was even more gentle and elegant.
In his right hand, Han Li held a White Feather Folding Fan, exuding a refined and elegant air. He was surrounded by chirping sparrows and swallows, like a touch of green amidst a sea of flowers.
He was enjoying the flower viewing and the scenery with a group of concubines, taking a stroll through the area.
It was clear to see that the concubines were quite fond of the newly built backyard garden, each wearing a face brimming with excitement.
When they reached the pond and began striking a wooden fish upon the shore, the golden carps would leap from the water, vying for the food.
The movement of fishes and lotuses in the pond reflected each other, with the mock hills and pavilions beside the pond mirrored in the water, and there were Han Li, Qiu Yueyao, Li Mingmeng, and others who appeared as if they had stepped out of a painting.
Subsequently, the group moved to another part of the garden, which not only had various precious flowers but also rarities like peacocks and cranes.
At this moment, what was presented before everyone was a profusion of reds and purples.
Han Li had already planned for the backyard garden to feature views to be admired in all four seasons: the reds and purples of spring, the purples and scents of summer dresses, the red leaves and yellow chrysanthemums of autumn, and the proud snow-covered red plum blossoms of winter.
Half a month later, Han Li received a piece of news.
In the family’s main hall, Han Li sat at the upper seat, looking at his somewhat nervous descendants below, and spoke indifferently, “Is the news confirmed?”
With Han Li’s breakthrough to the Gangyuan Realm, his authority in front of his descendants had increased even more. Although he had never displayed the power of the Gangyuan Realm, he made all his descendants feel immensely pressured.
If not necessary, descendants would not bother Han Li, mainly because they felt too uncomfortable in his presence, trembling with fear and hardly daring to breathe heavily.
The one below was one of Han Li’s grandsons, quite capable, in charge of the Han Family’s newly developed pharmaceutical trade, and also responsible for the collection of Pill Formulas.
“It’s absolutely true, grandson wouldn’t dare to deceive the elder ancestor.”
Spoke Han Shigao cautiously. In recent years, he had felt that his grandfather’s authority was becoming increasingly profound, making him, a person with substantial power in the Han Family, feel uneasy. If not for the great importance of this matter, which affected his future position, Han Shigao wouldn’t have wished to meet with his elder ancestor.
Han Li waved his hand, and Han Shigao retreated. Han Li was left alone in the hall, deep in thought.
Should he go out for a walk?

chapters.title: Chapter 16 - 16 Reading the Changsheng Family, Savoring the Ancestor’s Life_1
chapters.content:
16 Chapter 16 Reading the Changsheng Family, Savoring the Ancestor’s Life_1
Translator: 549690339
Han Li had reached the pinnacle of the ninth layer of the Innate Realm by the age of 120, but it took him seventy-five years to break through to the Pihai Realm, a journey fraught with many twists and turns.
Even counting from his time in Lingjun City, that was forty-five years, and this was with Ninth Grade cultivation talent.
Now he was in the Gangyuan Realm, having spent only twelve years advancing from the Pihai Realm. He had also accumulated sixty-five years of cultivation, which, if fully assimilated, he estimated could elevate him to the mid-stage of the Gangyuan Realm.
His cultivation talent had also risen to the seventh grade. It could be said that the further he progressed, the faster his cultivation speed became—his rate of improvement was nothing short of meteoric!
Looking at the Changsheng Family, cherish the life of the elderly ancestor!
If most cultivators had such a cultivation speed, they would have been spirited and complacent, becoming renowned cultivational geniuses and living wildly outside, fearing that others might not know their great fortunes.
But Elder Han was different; he remained as steady as an old dog, avoiding drawing attention whenever possible, and had kept a low profile for many years. Others even thought he was just at the first or second level of the Pihai Realm. His secret to longevity was summed up in one word: “lay low!”
However, Han Li was now hesitant about whether to participate in the next auction at Fengyang Manor.
Fengyang Manor would hold a grand auction every fifty years, hosted by the Manor Lord and backed by the Daqian Empire.
Each auction was a lively event, with cultivators from surrounding manors flocking to bid on treasures they coveted.
The Han Family also had a presence in the city of Fengyang Manor and had gathered much information. At this upcoming auction, several pill formulas would be available, at least of the eighth grade, and there were even rumors of seventh-grade formulas.
This made Han Li very eager, as what he lacked most were pill formulas above the eighth grade.
This large-scale auction by Fengyang Manor was destined to attract many powerful individuals, with Pihai Realm and even Gangyuan Realm cultivators from the surrounding manors likely to attend.
Han Li wanted pill formulas, and so did others; this meant competition. Even if he successfully bid on a pill formula, Han Li would become well-known, which was a prospect he wasn’t too fond of.
As the saying goes, “The bigger the name, the bigger the target!”
Han Li often took history as his guide, admonishing himself not to be too ostentatious. He aimed to break through quietly, live long quietly, be stable in all things, and be sure of his actions.
The laws of the Daqian Empire were quite strict. One could not initiate combat within the cities at will; otherwise, the enforcement teams would apprehend or even kill the offenders.
Outside the city walls, however, there were far fewer rules. Murder and loot were common occurrences, and if one were killed and robbed, it was only due to insufficient strength or bad luck.
The Qian Dynasty wouldn’t intervene in such matters, nor did it have the energy to do so, as long as there were no disturbances within the various cities.
The former Emperor Qian was incredibly domineering and unfathomable in strength. His reign marked another golden age for the Qian Dynasty, but he offended too many powers.
The current Emperor Qian lacked sufficient strength and finesse to stabilize the vast empire, leading to the downturn of the Qian Dynasty. If not for the fear of the True Martial Realm ancestors hidden within the Qian Dynasty, the Kurong Sect, Yinyang Sect, and Da Jing Empire would have already taken action.
Although Han Li had stayed in Lingjun City all these years, he had always been dedicated to gathering intelligence, giving him a sense that he understood the world without stepping outside. He had clearly noticed the declining governance of the Qian Dynasty, predicting significant events within the next two to five hundred years.
If Han Li successfully auctioned for the pill formulas, he would inevitably offend those vying for them. It was probable that they might attack him outside the city. Even if Han Li could easily retaliate, it would expose his strength, unless he found a deserted place to strike.
If the assailant backed by powerful forces went to attack Han Li and did not return for a long time, any subsequent investigation could still implicate Han Li.
“Alas, everything comes with risks. How can there be no risk at all?” Han Li lamented.
“`
Even if one were just scraping by in Lingjun City, keeping a low profile, there would still be immeasurable risks involved. It is possible for a battle between powerful beings to impact the city or for an old demon to slaughter the inhabitants in pursuit of dark cultivation…
However, such events are extremely improbable, and the associated risk is much lower compared to other dangers.
Since the risks are significant and the variables many, Han Li decided not to participate in the large auction held by Fengyang Manor after all. If it took a little more time, he would eventually collect enough pill formulas.
Having made his decision, Han Li no longer worried. Whatever time the auction was held or whatever heaven-defying treasures appeared, it was all irrelevant to him.
In the following two months, Han Li still stayed in Han Mansion, spending his days appreciating flowers, arranging them, crafting pills, reading, handling jade, watching dances…
One day, while leisurely enjoying the flowers with his ladies, Han Li suddenly received a system notification.
“You have fifty descendants with cultivation talent, you gain an additional twenty years of cultivation, you obtain one seventh-grade Lifespan Extension Pill, and you gain thirty years of artifact refining experience,” it said.
“Huh?”
Han Li blinked, realizing that there was something good among the rewards this time.
Thirty years of artifact refining experience could almost make him an eighth-grade Artifact Refiner, opening another revenue stream for the Han Family and temporarily solving the problem that plagued him.
If the spirit stones earned from selling pills were not enough, then he could sell weapons! Weapons are essential; no matter whether one is in the Innate Realm, Pihai Realm, or below, in order to enhance power, one has to buy several weapons.
If a cultivator has a powerful weapon, they could even challenge opponents beyond their level.
Han Li accepted the thirty years of artifact refining experience, which took some time to fully absorb, granting him a wealth of refining knowledge, techniques, and other experiences.
He stored the additional twenty years of cultivation as well. His account now had eighty-five years of cultivation saved, exceeding half of his target amount.
He kept the Lifespan Extension Pill. Although it was only a seventh-grade pill and each could only extend life by ten years and was only effective for cultivators below the God Refining Realm, its value was also very high. If auctioned, it would be worth at least a thousand mid-grade spiritual stones, which equaled one hundred thousand lower-grade spiritual stones.
Poor saps in the Innate Realm shouldn’t even dream about it, while those at the peak of the Pihai Realm might consider it. However, treasures like the Lifespan Extension Pill were invaluable and hard to come by.
Great Masters in the Gang Yuan Realm had more money and could easily buy a Lifespan Extension Pill.
Over the years, Han Li had gradually acquired quite a number of seventh-grade Lifespan Extension Pills. He had used some on his concubines, and with this one, he only had four left in storage.
He wouldn’t easily sell such treasures as Lifespan Extension Pills; otherwise, he might attract the attention of some old Gang Yuan Realm cultivators with not much time left.
Soon, Han Li drafted a list, all concerning refining materials and blueprints, and had the descendants of the Han Family start collecting them.
Crafting pills requires pill formulas, and naturally, artifact crafting needs blueprints. Han Li was now equivalent to an eighth-grade Artifact Refiner; he couldn’t just look at a weapon and be able to reproduce it on the spot.
The steps in artifact crafting, the techniques, the proportion of materials needed, if any of these was off, the artifact might not be successfully crafted.
To craft some powerful spiritual artifacts or magical treasures, formation scripts had to be carved into them to enhance their potency.
In legend, divine weapons and immortal artifacts hold boundless power. With a single strike, they can turn the world upside down, a might Han Li could hardly imagine.
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 17 - 17 Impending Storm_1
chapters.content:
17 Chapter 17 Impending Storm_1
Translator: 549690339
Two months later.
Han Li walked out of the Artifact Refining Pavilion with a smile on his face.
This time, he had successfully refined an alchemy furnace and an artifact refining furnace, both of Supreme Grade yellow-level spiritual artifacts, which greatly increased the efficiency of his alchemy and artifact refining.
With these two suitable spiritual artifacts, his success rate of producing elixirs would increase by at least thirty percent, and the speed of artifact refining could also improve by roughly thirty percent.
Now, Han Li spent two hours each day on alchemy and artifact refining to earn enough spirit stones for the Han Family. The rest of the time, he would spend with his concubines, discussing which fruit tasted better, whether honey peaches or mandarins, or…
Han Li felt that his current life was quite fulfilling, every day he had to impart teachings and produce elixirs and refine artifacts for his family, as well as prune the vibrant flowers in the garden. If he hadn’t broken through to the Gang Yuan Realm, he feared he might not have enough energy for all these tasks.
Han Li’s treasury was now empty, so he had to spend more time on alchemy and artifact refining.
Enjoying the attentiveness of the women around him and looking at their lovely, blooming faces, Han Li felt very content. Wasn’t such a life better than constant fighting and killing?
“Husband, have you heard that there’s unrest within the empire lately?” Li Mingmeng said with a frown, after feeding him a grape.
“Oh? Let’s hear it.”
Han Li looked thoughtful. He had been busy recently and hadn’t kept up with the news from the Daqian Empire.
Usually, he gathered information by having people from the Han Family go to the provincial cities’ Tianji Pavilion to buy it, which took ten days to and fro and the news was somewhat outdated.
The Tianji Pavilion was a very mysterious sect with branches in every provincial city of the Daqian Empire, specializing in selling information.
In theory, the Daqian Empire would not allow such a sect to exist, as it posed a certain threat to the Empire’s rule, but the Tianji Pavilion had survived to this day, mainly for two reasons.
It was a very ancient and mysterious sect, even more ancient than the Ancient Empire, the oldest empire in the Xuan Domain.
The Ancient Empire was the foremost among the four great empires of the Xuan Domain and the number one force in the entire domain, standing firm for over sixteen thousand years, enduring through the vast changes of time and the vicissitudes of dynasties.
The Daqian Empire was the youngest among the four great empires, having been established for just over three thousand years, and relatively speaking, had the shallowest foundation.
From ancient times, the Tianji Pavilion had remained neutral, only selling information and never interfering in other affairs or the struggles between forces, therefore, the major powers tolerated the presence of the Tianji Pavilion to a great extent.
The other reason was that the foundation of the Tianji Pavilion was unfathomably deep.
This was a power older than the Ancient Empire, always shrouded in mystery, never meddling in power struggles, just earning spiritual stone resources through information, and who knew how many old monsters were hidden within?
The branches of the Tianji Pavilion were not limited to the Daqian Empire; they were spread throughout the Xuan Domain and even throughout the eight domains and two seas of the Qianyuan Divine Province, making it one of the most profoundly established forces in the entire province.
Earning so many spirit stones and having astonishing wealth to stand, at least, for twenty thousand years without falling, the foundation of Tianji Pavilion was truly frightening.
Once, a top-ranked sect set its sights on the wealth of the Tianji Pavilion and attempted to seize it, only to be exterminated overnight. It was rumored that in that top sect, there was a warrior at the True Martial Realm who was an Emperor Wu.
After that battle, no one dared to offend the Tianji Pavilion again, and no one dared to provoke this colossal entity lurking beneath the surface.
Since the Tianji Pavilion remained neutral and only dealt in information without meddling in the struggles between major forces, these powers also tacitly approved the existence of the Tianji Pavilion.
After feeding Han Li two incredibly sweet grapes, Li Mingmeng then continued, “Recently, a White Lotus Cult has emerged within the Daqian Empire, preaching about the ‘Mother of Non-Birth, Void Hometown’ and has been spreading their teachings vigorously in Huozhou, affecting five or six provinces, expanding very rapidly.”
“After the Daqian Empire reacted, they declared it a heretical cult, convinced that it was deluding and coercing the populace with thoughts of rebellion, and so Emperor Qian decreed an immediate purge in Huozhou.”
“The Protector General of Huozhou led four God Refining Realm masters and the Huozhou army to besiege them, but they were defeated, reportedly falling into an ambush. The Protector General of Huozhou was seriously injured, two of the God Refining Realm masters died, and two were injured, with countless casualties in the Huozhou army.”
“Now, the whole of Huozhou is in turmoil, with rumors saying that the White Lotus Cult is advancing towards Huozhou City.”
Han Li’s expression changed sharply upon hearing this, sensing the gravity of the situation. What was this White Lotus Cult that had emerged out of nowhere, capable of contending with the Huozhou army?
In the Daqian Empire, each province has an undetermined number of prefectures, generally ranging between twenty to thirty, like Leizhou with twenty-three prefectures, Huozhou with twenty-five prefectures, and so on.
The fact that the White Lotus Cult could swiftly sweep across five or six prefectures certainly indicated something fishy behind the scenes, possibly the workings of a top-tier power from the Xuan Domain.
