chapters.title: Chapter 100 - 100 Departure_l
chapters.content:
Chapter 100: Departure_l
Translator: 549690339
Today, Spirit Balance City was especially bustling.
In the past, such commotion was due to the Han Family’s patriarch taking a concubine; today’s stir was also related to the Han Family, as they were set to
officially relocate.
Within Spirit Balance City, countless citizens hurried to spread the word, all making their way to the city outskirts, hoping to make one last effort to persuade the Han Family to stay.
The numerous powers within the city were thrilled—finally, the Han Family was leaving. Those with marital ties to the Han Family sent emissaries to see them off, while other forces were already sharpening their knives, ready to divide up the Han Family’s territory.
Outside Spirit Balance City, a procession stretched over ten miles—the convoy of Han Mansion’s migration. Han Li’s concubines and descendants were all seated in carriages, surrounded by guards mounted on tall horses protecting them.
The entire convoy consisted of nearly five thousand people; Han Li’s concubines and descendants alone numbered six to seven hundred. Including their spouses and concubines, the count was even higher. The rest were maids, servants, guards, guest elders, and so forth.
The common folk who tried to approach were blocked by the guards, indifferent to their cries and pleas. Only relatives by marriage were allowed to come closer to bid farewell.
This might be the last time they would see each other in this life; separated by several provinces, those below the Pihai Realm could neither contact nor meet.
Han Li’s carriage was positioned in the middle of the convoy, a deliberate arrangement on his part to take care of the entire procession and prevent any loss from ambushes.
To Han Li, the death of maids and guards was not a cause for grief. With some gold and Spirit Stones, he could recruit more. They all had signed contracts; even in death, their families would receive compensation, and they had been given a generous resettlement fee before the move.
These maids and guards were either orphans or not their families’ only child, nor did they have wives or children in Spirit Balance City, so they could follow the Han Mansion to Yuanzhou.
If Han Li lost his concubines or descendants, however, he would be grieved, for they were the foundation for establishing the family in Yuanzhou and the continuous source of advancement in cultivation and rewards.
Han Li’s carriage, while outwardly no different from the others, was many times more comfortable inside, with top-notch materials and decorations throughout.
Each carriage in the convoy was drawn by two precious steeds, each containing a trace of the Demon Clan’s bloodline and possessing Rebirth Realm strength, capable of traveling more than five thousand miles a day.
The carriages of certain key figures were drawn by two precious steeds with True Qi Realm strength, and Han Li’s carriage was even better, with two steeds at the Innate Realm, practically members of the Demon Clan themselves.
It wasn’t that Han Li couldn’t buy better steeds, but that he shouldn’t.
Purchasing a large number of steeds at the Innate or even Pihai Realm would easily draw attention to Han Li. The Han Family’s moving procession was enormous and not quiet.
The greater the number, the more likely they were to attract trouble, leading to continuous problems on the migration route—something Han Li did not wish to see.
Moreover, purchasing such steeds required strength—a Great Master at the Gangyuan Realm was not enough; a genuine God Refining Realm elder would need to intervene.
In Han Li’s view, there was little use in buying them—they were just for pulling carriages. Should they encounter a crisis, what good would the strength of the Pihai or Gangyuan Realm do?
If attacked, and he couldn’t beat the assailants, he could only wrap up everyone and flee.
With combat ability approaching the threshold of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, escaping with five thousand people was not difficult for him; the speed would not decrease much, and at least those in the later stages of the Myriad Phenomena Realm wouldn’t be able to catch up.
This would fully reveal Han Li’s strength, but under such circumstances, there was no further need for secrecy.
For now, Han Li didn’t want to expose himself. If he were to wrap up everyone and flee to Yuanzhou, it would cause a huge commotion and countless people would witness it.
Even if he set up a Formation outside of Han Mansion to hide his tracks, and wrapped up everyone from within to flee, and no one in Spirit Balance City saw it, it would still be exposed.
Once the people of Han Mansion settled in Yuanzhou and began to expand, they would inevitably attract the attention of the powers in Yuanzhou, who would investigate their origins. Smaller powers might not be able to trace the Han Family back to Leizhou, but larger powers certainly could.
Not to mention the inscrutable Tianji Pavilion. By connecting all the dots and conducting a little analysis, they could deduce most of Han Li’s strength, and once that information was marked and available for purchase, he would be fully exposed.
Leizhou wished even more for a spatial treasure that could store people; if he had a pocket dimension, a small world of his own, that would be just perfect.
The Han Family could develop directly within this small world, and he himself could simply find a remote corner to establish a cave dwelling and scrape by. By setting up a warning formation on the outside, he could then happily cultivate within the small world.
In that way, he could hide out in the small world until the end of time. When he reemerged, he would be invincible. Just thinking about it was wonderful.
If he encountered any danger, he could just take the small world and run, an easy and convenient way to greatly reduce the risks the family’s development might face.
Unfortunately, Leizhou didn’t have one.
This carriage housed only Leizhou himself, making it convenient for him to act during the journey. When necessary, he could summon the beautiful consorts to come in and spend some time playing games to pass the time.
Now, he lay down in a comfortable position, as his Spiritual Sense surged out, gradually covering the entirety of Fengyang Manor and bringing everything into his view.
After confirming there was no danger, Leizhou then gave out the orders.
The next moment, upon receiving the order, the Han Mansion’s caravan started moving, and the Han Family began their official relocation.
Countless people in Lingjun City watched this scene with various expressions and thoughts—some were jubilant, some cursed loudly, some were mournfully saying goodbye, and others were endlessly grateful….
No matter what they were thinking, nothing could interfere with Leizhou’s decision or disrupt the Han Family’s migration.
When necessary, Leizhou wouldn’t hesitate to kill without mercy; he had never been a thoroughly good person from the beginning.
From Qingzhou to Yuanzhou, the journey was long, with Fengyang Manor situated in the south of Qingzhou, and the location Leizhou chose in Yuanzhou was a place to the east, named Yonchang Manor.
The entire route of migration involved Qingzhou, Qingzhou, Jizhou, and Yuanzhou, covering a journey of approximately two million six hundred thousand miles.
Even if the entire caravan travelled at the speed of five thousand miles per day, it would take 520 days, nearly a year and a half, and probably two years to reach Yonchang Manor in Yuanzhou if anything happened en route.
Leizhou thought this pace was acceptable, and the time spent was not excessive, given the scale of the migration spanning several provinces.
During the migration, it would not affect the expansion of the family. Before moving, the Han Mansion had already prepared an abundance of various resources, ensuring the journey would not lack supplies.
Leizhou estimated that before reaching Yonchang Manor in Yuanzhou, the number of his descendants would exceed seven hundred, and the number of descendants with talents, over two hundred.
Then his strength would further increase, advancing him to the Myriad Phenomena Realm and making him a Great Grandmaster.
With the significant increase in strength, he would be better able to protect his family and safely migrate to Yonchang Manor in Yuanzhou.
Before that, he needed to ensure the family’s safety on the migration route and clear out any tough obstacles.
He would scout ahead with his Spiritual Sense on the predetermined route. His Spiritual Sense covered an area of two hundred thousand miles in radius, rivaling many Great Grandmasters in the Myriad Phenomena Realm. Unless they were very powerful Grandmasters who deliberately concealed themselves, he would be able to detect them.
Leizhou didn’t think that those at the later or peak stages of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, nor the Gurus in the Void Realm would attack the Han Family’s migrating caravan.
After all, Grandmasters cared about their face and reputation. Who would attack the caravan of a small family?
How many treasures could a small family possess? Could they all add up to ten thousand Spirit Stones?
Those in the Hollow Void Stage wouldn’t spare them a glance, not even the Real People in the God Refining Realm, though it might be a potential windfall for a Great Master in the Gangyuan Realm..

chapters.title: Chapter 101: The Beginning of Taking Off_1
chapters.content:
Chapter 101: The Beginning of Taking Off_1
Translator: 549690339
The convoy stretching for ten miles majestically left Lingjun City, heading northward. It would pass through six manors before reaching the border between Leizhou and Qingzhou.
Within Leizhou territory, it was still relatively safe. Once they reached the border, they would venture through a vast desolate area, which was also the place most likely to be attacked.
Many bandits were entrenched along the borders of each province, and those that had managed to survive had various factors influencing their existence.
After reaching Qingzhou, they would travel in the northeast direction, passing through eight manors, crossing over six hundred thousand miles, and then finally arrive at the Qingji Border.
Upon entering Jizhou, they had to detour to avoid the Province City, hence they would pass through nine manors, with a journey of over eight hundred thousand miles.
After reaching Yuanzhou, by passing through another seven manors, they would arrive at Yonchang Manor, the place Han Li had chosen, with about five hundred thousand miles of travel within Yuanzhou.
This was the migration route devised by Han Li, prioritizing safer roads, preferring to spend more time rather than take risks.
As time went by, the migrating caravan proceeded all the way to Zhending Manor without encountering any dangers along the way, thanks to Han Li’s Spiritual Sense paving the way.
Major troubles were diverted around, while minor issues were handled by the family guards or descendants. For this move, Han Li even specifically recruited a few cultivators from the Pihai Realm.
With the display of his Gang Yuan Realm cultivation, coupled with the temptation of Pihai Realm cultivation enriching elixirs, Spirit Stones, and Pihai Realm weapons, these cultivators agreed after only slight hesitation.
Due to the sheer size of the migrating team, stretching for ten miles, they still attracted quite a bit of attention along the way.
Upon learning that Han Mansion’s purpose was to leave Leizhou, those smaller forces breathed a sigh of relief, as even the strongest among these forces were only at the Pihai and Gang Yuan Realms—if the Han Family moved in, it would encroach on their resources.
Larger forces, on the other hand, were indifferent. The Han Family’s relocation was still within their territories nominally under the rule of the Daqian Empire, but in reality governed by various sects.
Leizhou and Qingzhou were connected by three manors with checkpoints for travel between them, which were Zhenwen Manor, Zhending Manor, and Zhenyi Manor.
Traveling through Zhenwen Manor into Qingzhou would allow quick access to Huozhou; traveling through Zhending Manor into Qingzhou would allow quick access to Jizhou; and traveling through Zhenyi Manor into Qingzhou would allow quick access to Luzhou.
When the migrating team arrived about two hundred miles from Zhou Pass, it was already the hour of Xu, getting late, so the caravan stopped for rest, planning to enter Qingzhou the next day.
The massive convoy compacted, forming concentric circles around Han Li’s carriage at the center, with a large number of guards patrolling on precious horses in the outermost ring.
Within the convoy, there was approximately a two-meter gap between each circle, where maids shuttled back and forth, carrying various foods and fruits to deliver to the masters in their carriages.
In the center of the convoy, Han Li was also busy, at the moment instructing his descendants.
Before him were Han Yonglin, Han Yongyun, and other descendants who had just turned eight, as well as Han Yongfan, Han Yongyan, and others who had already embarked on the path of cultivation.
With the resources provided by the Han Family, those with better aptitude had already cultivated to the True Qi of the Third Realm, while those with lesser talent were lingering in the First and Second Realms.
Han Li had over one hundred and sixty descendants with innate gifts; there were many below eight years old, and even more above eight, numbering about a hundred.
The migration was expected to take two years, and Han Li did not wish for the prime-aged descendants to miss out on cultivation time, so he had no choice but to teach and instruct them on the journey.
As for his beauties, they needed to be privately taught and imbued with essence. Among his concubines, those with good aptitude had already cultivated to the Pihai Realm, the rest were concentrated in the Innate Realm, and only those new concubines who had been taken in recently were below the Innate Realm.
Because of the Body-Cultivating Furnace, every time Han Li imparted essence to them, not only did it enhance their cultivation, but it also improved their aptitude, gradually accelerating their cultivation speed.
Presently, even the concubines with the poorest aptitude had reached Fourth Grade, the majority were at Seventh Grade, a few were at Sixth Grade, and as for Fifth Grade, there were only two—the sisters Lin Yiwu and Lin Yiyin, with Lin Yiyin’s aptitude only recently upgraded.
Not only were the concubines’ aptitudes improving, Han Li’s own aptitude was also on the rise. In this period, not many gifted descendants were born, but the Body-Cultivating Furnace had significantly enhanced his talents.
Han Li had reviewed his aptitude on the system panel; it was steadily increasing and had now reached Fifth Grade 12%, which was much higher than when he first advanced to Fifth Grade aptitude.
What he regretted was that the Body-Cultivating Furnace could only raise a cultivator’s aptitude to a max of Fourth Grade, and it would require a vast amount of time.
“Yonglin, Yongyun, Yongfu… how is the cultivation of the Five Elements
Formula I taught you? Have you made any entry into it?”
Looking at his descendants, Han Li called out their names one by one and inquired about their cultivation progress.
The Five Elements Formula was an Earth-Level Lower Rank cultivation technique, divided into eight layers, and could be cultivated up to the Hollow Void Stage. Han Li temporarily used it as the foundational cultivation method for his family.
As for the earlier Sacred Heart Scripture, it was only of Profound Rank median grade, divided into six layers, and could only be cultivated up to the Gangyuan Realm. It was taught to family guards and Guest Elders, of course, requiring them to make corresponding contributions and establish sufficient merits.
“Father, I have already cultivated to the late stage of the first layer,” Han Yonglin said excitedly, with a somewhat proud expression, head held high, waiting for Han Li’s praise.
Reaching the late stage of the first layer meant he had cultivated to the late stage of the Body Forging Realm, and this left Han Li somewhat astonished; a Fourth Grade talent was indeed remarkable.
He himself had taken a full two years to break through to the late stage of the Body Forging Realm, which was related to starting his cultivation at the age of sixteen, having poor talent, inferior cultivation methods, and lacking cultivation resources.
Han Yonglin achieved such results in less than a month, which, apart from having good talent, was also related to having good cultivation methods, abundant cultivation resources, and guidance from Han Li, a Grandmaster, during his optimal cultivation period.
“Very good, much stronger than your father in his time,” Han Li spared no praise.
“Father, father, I am also close to reaching the late stage of the first layer,” Han Yongyun hurriedly said, also seeking Han Li’s commendation.
Han Li could see at a glance that his cultivation was at the sixth layer of Body Forging Realm, which was also quite good, so he praised him as well. “Father, I’ve only cultivated to the early stage of the first layer.” “Father, I just reached the mid-stage of the first layer.”
“Father…”
Han Yongfu and the other descendants spoke up in turn, but their expressions were somewhat inferior, and compared to Han Yonglin and Han Yongyun, they were far behind.
Han Li understood quite well; after all, these descendants only had talent at the Seventh or Eighth Grade, and they were still teaching Earth Rank practice methods, which were relatively difficult to master. If it weren’t for his guidance, it would probably take even longer to see the progress they were now making.
For those descendants with lesser talent, Han Li took an encouraging approach, letting them know that continuous diligent practice would also lead to achievements in the future.
This was not just talk; once they moved to Yuanzhou, he planned to find the Rebirth Flower as quickly as possible, refine the Rebirth Pills, and then all descendants with talent could raise their talent to the Fourth Grade, reaching the same level as Han Yonglin.
He was not ready to reveal this just yet; he still needed to take secrecy measures and prepare everything properly before enhancing the talents of his descendants. Fortunately, he already had a detailed plan in place, waiting only for the move to Yuanzhou.
Yuanzhou, that was where the rise of the Han Family would begin.
In Yuanzhou, a tremendously large cultivation family would emerge.
By then, the Han Family would be the true power behind the scenes in the Daqian Empire, and perhaps even in the Xuan Domain.
After resolving the cultivation doubts raised by Han Yonglin, Han Yongfu, and the other descendants, he said, “Those with good talent mustn’t be arrogant, and those with lesser talent shouldn’t be discouraged. Your father also didn’t have high talent but achieved what he has today through relentless diligence.” “You must remember one sentence, ‘In the future, all things are possible.”‘
“I will do my best to create a relatively fair cultivation environment for you all. Just wait and see,” Han Li said.
Han Li turned to Han Yongfan, Han Yongyan, and others, and said, “The same goes for you.”
“Yes, Father,” Han Yonglin, Han Yongfan, and the others replied excitedly, their eyes filled with admiration when they looked at Han Li.
Outsiders thought their father was a Great Master of the Gangyuan Realm, but they knew that their father was a True Being of the God Refining Realm, incredibly powerful.
This was a secret they held in their hearts, one that they would never speak of to others..

chapters.title: Chapter 102 - 102 1’ll Deliver It Personally_1
chapters.content:
Chapter 102 - 102 1’ll Deliver It Personally_1
Chapter 102: 1’ll Deliver It Personally_1
Translator: 549690339
Yuanzhou, Xuanshi Manor.
In the manor city, within a tall-gated, large courtyard.
Amidst a sea of bamboo, in a tranquil environment, a woman in a purple dress and a beauty in a yellow dress were sitting opposite each other; the woman in the purple dress was brewing tea.
Her delicate, snow-white hand poured carefully selected fine water into a spirit pot, then she snapped her fingers, and a flame appeared beneath the purple-golden pot.
When the water was heated but not yet fully boiling, she added some top-quality spiritual tea leaves to the pot.
As the tea and water melded, the second boil produced froth; small froths were tiny tea flowers, the larger froths indicated the essence of the tea.
At this moment, she scooped out the froth and placed it in a ready bowl, reserving it for later; as she continued to boil the tea, the tea and water blended further, churning into waves, and reaching the third boil.
The woman in the purple dress then poured the froth, reserved from the second boil, into the tea, and since there were only two of them, she didn’t add much.
After the tea was ready, the woman in the purple dress poured the tea into two cups evenly, symbolizing the sharing of both fortunes and hardships.
“Please,” the woman in the purple dress gestured.
The beauty in the yellow dress nodded slightly, her long pale hands taking the cup and instantly, a refreshing fragrance wafted toward her, pleasant and delightful. She gently took a sip.
She couldn’t help but hold her breath, waiting until the tea slid down her throat, then she slightly pursed her small cherry lips and exhaled slowly through her nose, savoring the origin of the tea’s fragrance.
“Excellent tea,” the beauty in the yellow dress appraised.
She had already smelled the aromatic tea while it was brewing, and after drinking it, she felt the aroma was full-bodied, dispersing through her mouth and throat.
The woman in the purple dress put down her cup, her charming face breaking into a smile, “I must say, the Human Clan has a way of enjoyment that we from the Demon Clan simply cannot compare to.”
“Take this tea, for instance; it’s a form of high art that we from the Demon Clan do not understand. We’re far behind the Human Clan.”
The beauty in the yellow dress nodded. Since arriving in the Daqian Empire, they were almost dazzled by its splendid world, with all the wonderful things the Human Clan had to offer leaving them wanting more.
In the capital city of the Daqian Empire, both women were adept at enjoying life. After they escaped to Yuanzhou and found some stability, they reverted back to their real selves.
They preferred to stay in a wealthy and bustling manor city over living meagerly in the towns and villages—truly, it is easier to go from frugality to extravagance than from extravagance to frugality.
“Shall we move on?” the woman in the purple dress suddenly asked.
The beauty in the yellow dress fell silent for a moment, then said, “It depends on the situation. If there’s no trouble, we’ll stay in Xuanshi City.”
In a moment of anger, she had caused trouble in the capital city of Daqian, drawing the attention of the Jingye Office. Now they were wanted all over.
However, this wasn’t challenging for the two women; they were highly skilled in cultivation and were experts in the art of disguise, having already altered their appearances.
Capital City of Da Qian.
In the finely decorated boudoir of a Prime Minister’s manor.
“Those two little foxes, I wonder if they’ve escaped.”
She put down her embroidery and quietly murmured to herself, recalling a scene she had chanced upon earlier.
Bearing in mind that the two women were inherently good and that they were somewhat connected to her by race, the peerless beauty had secretly assisted them.
“I never thought I’d see the day when I would enjoy helping others,” she scoffed at herself.
In her past life, with her temperament, she wouldn’t have bothered with such trifles, and she was known to have a bad temper.
Yet, after reincarnation, she came to understand many things and her personality gradually changed. She lived a peaceful life in the Prime Minister’s manor, and even though she was highly skilled in cultivation, she acted like a delicate woman without any skills.
“The time is near, just a little longer, and my planning will come to fruition,” the peerless beauty mused to herself. She had been quietly laying out many schemes lately.
Prince Wu’an of the Daqian Empire coveted her treasure, but little did he know, she too was plotting to seize the empire’s treasures.
If played correctly, this move could bring her immense benefits, laying the foundation for her next step, and in this life, she might even have a chance to touch that realm.
The peerless beauty looked towards the direction of the Imperial Astronomer and sneered coldly.
She had been keenly aware of the Prophet of the Imperial Astronomer surveilling her previously, and she knew that the old thing harbored suspicions about her, though he was uncertain and lacked evidence.
“In the face of absolute power, all schemes and tricks are utterly useless,” said the peerless beauty with a light chuckle.
“Yue’er, are you there? I have something I’d like to talk to you about,” a voice sounded from outside the boudoir.
The peerless beauty’s eyebrows slightly furrowed; the visitor was her father of this lifetime, the current Prime Minister.
After a moment, the peerless beauty responded, “Hmm.”
The Prime Minister always held great respect for his daughter, but it seemed he truly had important matters this time…
Qingyun Manor, by Erhai Lake.
Lu Tianxiang was admiring her beauty in the mirror.
Because her main cultivation technique required the spreading of faith rather than rigorous cultivation practices, she was able to enhance her strength without the arduous task, a job taken care of by her subordinates.
Recruiting others was also hard work, and again, that was something her subordinates would handle; Lu Tianxiang would never bother herself with such matters.
Looking at herself in the mirror, Lu Tianxiang smiled, feeling she truly was a little temptress.
Her figure was stunningly gorgeous, extremely sultry, and quite mature; her curvaceous and graceful lines combined with a slender waist formed the perfect hot and sexy S-curve.
Her facial features were exquisitely crafted, and from her tender and smooth jade-like feet to her head, there wasn’t a single flaw in her beauty.
After admiring herself for a while, Lu Tianxiang put on a noble and elegant purple fairy dress, instantly covering up the tantalizing spring sights.
Having cultivated that technique, her already remarkable aura became even more extraordinary and sanctified. Now, dressed in these clothes, she appeared even more lofty and unreachable.
A fiery figure, breathtakingly beautiful features, and a holy demeanor—all combined perfectly in her, creating a stunningly beautiful woman, a temptress without equal.
After finishing, Lu Tianxiang’s figure disappeared and reappeared in the main hall of the Diancang Sect.
Looking at the Diancang Master bowing his head below, Lu Tianxiang’s indifferent voice resonated in the hall, “How is the situation?”
The Diancang Master, invigorated, replied respectfully, “Reporting to the Sect
Hierarch, all intelligence has been verified.”
“Qiu Xuan was badly injured on his way back from Dingyuan Manor to Fengyang Manor, and later died from his wounds. He had a wife and a daughter; his wife followed him in death, but his daughter is still alive.”
“Before Qiu Xuan died, he had his First Disciple go to Fengyang Manor to summon his good friend Han Li. The two met, and soon after, Qiu Xuan passed away.”
“Han Li took care of the funerals for Qiu Xuan and his wife, and then he took Qiu Yueyao back to Fengyang Manor.”
Lu Tianxiang felt relieved; it seemed that the Rebirth Pill formula was most likely in the hands of Han Li or Qiu Xuan’s daughter, Qiu Yueyao.
“What about the intelligence on Han Li?” Lu Tianxiang looked at the Diancang Master—if he dared to say he hadn’t found out, she was ready to slap him.
“Han Li, early Gangyuan Realm, once resided in Lingjun City of Fengyang
Manor and is known for taking concubines, often referred to as the ‘Concubine
Collecting Ancestor.’ He and Qiu Xuan were disciples from Tianxuan
Mountain.”
“Han Li is extremely cautious and usually stays within Lingjun City, not leaving often, probably due to Leizhou’s instability. Recently, he began relocating the Han Family to Yuanzhou, and now they have reached the border of Zhending
Manor and are about to enter Qingzhou territory.”
“Very well, you’ve done a good job with this,” said Lu Tianxiang.
Finally, a smile appeared on Lu Tianxiang’s face, making the dimly lit room seem brighter and the lights sparkle even more brilliantly.
“You go and bring Han Li back. I want to see him. Never mind, I will personally go to invite him,” said Lu Tianxiang, and with that, her figure vanished.
As a late-stage God Refining Realm cultivator, the Diancang Master found it very easy to catch an early-stage Gang Yuan cultivator, but for the sake of caution, Lu Tianxiang decided to take action herself.
She worried that the Diancang Master might make too much of a fuss, attracting the attention of Tianxuan Mountain or the Daqian Empire, which she did not want to deal with just yet. With her first level of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, she could easily capture an early Gang Yuan Realm cultivator without making a sound..

chapters.title: Chapter 103 - 103 Assassination 1
chapters.content:
Chapter 103: Assassination 1
Translator: 549690339
Migration Caravan.
After imparting his wisdom to a group of descendants, Han Li let them disperse, and then had a maid summon Lin Yiyin and Lin Yiwu, the sisterly duo of beauties.
Before long, the two stunning women made their way into his carriage, and Han Li was immediately enveloped by their fragrant scents.
While Lin Yiwu tried to maintain her composure, Lin Yiyin had already opened her snow-white arms and lunged into Han Li’s embrace.
“Husband-”
Lin Yiyin, having transformed from a maiden to a married woman, still retained some of her naiveté. Her voice was clear and melodious, sweetly whining as she wrapped Han Li in a tight hug and clung onto him akin to a koala.
Without hesitating, Han Li sat down to provide a more comfortable space for them, his arms enveloping Lin Yiyin in return, feeling engulfed by the mixture of orchid and cinnamon scents that coated her.
“Yiyin, what’s gotten into you?”
Han Li’s hand gently stroked Lin Yiyin’s back, with his other hand rubbing her head, he asked in a soft and soothing tone.
He had noticed that something was different about Lin Yiyin—she had always been proactive, but not quite to the extent she was displaying today.
With their bodies pressed closely together, as if to become one, Han Li could distinctly feel the soft and delicate pressure against his chest from the beauty in his arms.
“Yiwu.”
Gazing at Lin Yiwu who appeared somewhat shy, Han Li called out to her. Her face blushing, she nonetheless approached and quietly called him “Husband” with her cherry lips, then sat beside him.
Freeing one hand, Han Li wrapped it around Lin Yiwu’s slender waist and planted a kiss on her exquisite cheek, feeling an immense sense of satisfaction.
Both sisters were breathtakingly beautiful, with Lin Yiwu being cool and reserved, and Lin Yiyin being adorable and lively, making them even more attractive to Han Li than the twin sisters Chu Yumeng and Chu Yutong.
“Hehe- I’m just feeling very happy,” said Lin Yiyin, still perched on his thigh, her smile playful.
She felt overjoyed that evening after seeing her and her sister’s son displaying exceptional potential, and hearing Han Li praise their son. Witnessing Han Li mentor their many descendants filled her heart with joy.
Han Li smiled and nodded, then brought up serious matters, “I’ve called you here tonight to pass on knowledge and techniques, as your cultivation levels are still too low.”
“You and Yiwu both possess fifth-grade talents now, and there’s a very good chance you’ll break through to the Hollow Realm in the future. You need to cultivate more diligently, especially you, Yiyin; you need to put in extra effort.”
Lin Yiwu responded with a soft ‘Mhm.”
“Ah? When did I become a fifth-grade talent?” Lin Yiyin blinked her sapphire-like eyes in confusion.
Han Li chuckled, recalling how she never paid attention to such matters, and explained, “Haven’t you noticed that your cultivation speed has increased recently?”
“I did notice! I thought it was all thanks to you, my husband, as you often share your knowledge with me and my sister,” Lin Yiyin said matter-of-factly.
“You’re not wrong in saying that,” Han Li replied with a smile.
Han Li remembered that Lin Yiyin’s advancement in talent was indeed the result of their sessions when he transmitted techniques to the sisters.
“But I don’t want to cultivate, it should be fine for you and my sister to focus on your own cultivation, right? With you two protecting me, there’s really no need for me to improve my abilities,” Lin Yiyin said, shaking her little head, causing her hair to cascade in waves.
“You still need to make an effort, there are times when your husband won’t be around, and your current cultivation level is not enough to protect you,” Han Li said as he flicked his finger lightly. A considerable amount of Gang Yuan silently flowed out, forming an invisible sound barrier around the outside of the carriage.
“I will cultivate even harder,” said Lin Yiwu, her red lips pursed.
“Let’s not talk about this tonight. Let me see how your cultivation is progressing. Is the Five Elements Formula advancing smoothly? Do you have any issues with cultivation? Or are there other problems…” Han Li inquired with concern.
“Husband, you’re too fast, slow down, I didn’t quite catch that. Yes, just like that, take it slow, and I’ll understand,” Lin Yiyin’s voice rang out.
Perhaps due to her natural talent, Lin Yiyin was more perceptive and understood quicker. Throughout Han Li’s instruction, she remained silent, only occasionally calling out a sweet “Husband-
Two hours later, Han Li finally finished giving the two women their private lessons, and sensing that their cultivation had improved, he saw their radiant, beautiful faces and felt that his efforts were all worth it.
Han Li was about to say something when he suddenly frowned and changed his words, “Yiwu, Yiyin, you two go back first. I still have some things to deal with.
“But I really want to hug my husband to sleep-” Lin Yiyin cooed, sending a tingling sensation through Han Li.
“Good girl-”
Han Li gently stroked her fair face and pecked both women on their cheeks, giving Lin Yiwu a knowing look.
Left with no choice, Lin Yiwu pulled Lin Yiyin away with her.
As the sisters left, Han Li’s expression immediately turned grim. Without hesitation, his figure vanished from the carriage.
Night was the most dangerous time, and no matter what he was doing, his spiritual sense always covered a wide area, guarding against any potential crises.
Just then, a formidable presence had entered the range of his spiritual sense at an extremely fast pace and was heading towards his location, instantly alerting Han Li.
They hadn’t left Leizhou yet and already a powerful individual had come to intercept him—judging by the revealed aura and speed, it was a Guru in the Void Realm.
What was key was that this person was not any Grandmaster he knew of. Han Li had intelligence on all the Grandmasters from Leizhou, as well as from Qingzhou and Huozhou.
The comer was clearly harboring ill intentions.
He didn’t know why a Grandmaster would suddenly attack the Han Family’s convoy, but he knew he had to nip the danger in the bud.
Thus, Han Li sprang into action.
Upon first advancing to the Hollow Void Stage, his spiritual sense could cover a radius of twenty thousand li. Having reached the Peak of the Hollow Realm, it now spanned two hundred thousand li, comparable to a Great Grandmaster in the later stages of the Myriad Phenomena Realm.
At full speed, he could traverse eight thousand li in one step, almost fifty thousand li in the span of a breath, many times faster than a Hollow Sect Master. With his combat ability, as long as he detected the enemy, he could swiftly arrive and vanquish them.
As long as he didn’t use techniques like the God Slaying Sword or Xuantian
Punch or any unique skills from Tianxuan Mountain, no one would suspect Han Li. He had several martial arts techniques that had not yet been revealed, and the entirety of his martial arts skillset had not been exposed either.
One was a mysterious expert with the combat ability of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, and the other was a Great Master who had only recently reached the Gangyuan Realm. The difference between the two spanned several Big Realms.
Meanwhile, Lu Tianxiang was on her way.
After leaving the Diancang Sect, she traveled overnight, chasing under the stars, determined not to let that Han Li escape.
She suspected that Han Li’s decision to move the Han Family was not due to concerns that a great battle would erupt in Leizhou; after all, Han Li’s status was too low to be involved in matters at the level of Prince Wu’an.
Instead, it was likely that he sensed someone searching for Qiu Xuan and possibly tracking the Pill Formula, which was in his hands. Frightened, Han Li might be intending to flee Leizhou and head to Yuanzhou, far away, to avoid the trouble.
“True to his reputation as an ancestor with many concubines, he regards his beauties so importantly.”
Thinking of the reports that Han Li took all his beauties and descendants with him when he moved, Lu Tianxiang couldn’t help but sneer.
At such a critical moment, he still couldn’t let go of those beauties and made his escape with them—how deeply he was enamored by beauty.
However, this was convenient for her in capturing Han Li. If he had fled alone, abandoning his property and beauties, she would have to spend much time searching and might not even find him.
PS: Due to certain reasons, this book has been renamed to “Surviving in the World of Immortal Martial Arts and Marrying for Longevity”!

chapters.title: Chapter 104 - 104 Unethical Martial Conduct_l
chapters.content:
Chapter 104: Unethical Martial Conduct_l
Translator: 549690339
At this moment, Lu Tianxiang had changed her attire and makeup, resembling a dignified and luxurious middle-aged matron, clad entirely in black with a veil covering her face, right down to her pink, bare feet that were now encased in combat boots.
She was only displaying the cultivation of the Hollow Void Stage, flying at the speed consistent with that stage, and being quite cautious not to pass over the territories of the major factions.
Lu Tianxiang did not wish to reveal herself, as being at the Myriad Phenomena Realm was too conspicuous. If Leizhou harbored any Great Grandmasters of the Myriad Phenomena Realm from Da Qian lying in wait, it was very likely they would detect her.
She was the notorious Mother Wusheng, and if recognized, she would be hunted by Da Qian again, and the foundation she had painstakingly accumulated would have to be abandoned.
But what Mother Wusheng could not contemplate was that the Cultivator of the Gangyuan Realm she mentioned possessed combat ability comparable to that of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, had Spiritual Sense akin to those in the middle to late stages of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, and was constantly covering an area over fifty thousand miles with his Spiritual Sense, having discovered her long ago.
After all, which Great Grandmaster would constantly cover a vast area with their Spiritual Sense? That would be quite taxing on their mental strength
As Lu Tianxiang traveled, her Spiritual Sense usually only maintained coverage within ten thousand miles, since a wider range consumed more mental strength.
Lu Tianxiang flew thousands of miles forward, then suddenly came to a halt mid-air without advancing further, her eyebrows tightly furrowed.
A hundred miles ahead of her, a person stood atop a mountain peak, with their back to her, hands clasped behind them, also dressed in black.
Her Spiritual Sense stretched forth in an attempt to probe the person’s identity but was blocked by their Spiritual Sense, unable to cover the area at all.
The person posed a considerable threat to her, quite possibly being a Great Grandmaster of the Myriad Phenomena Realm. Suddenly appearing ahead, barring her path—could they be coming for her?
Lu Tianxiang considered taking a detour, but no matter how she moved, that person seemed to firmly lock onto her, confirming her suspicion that they had come specifically for her.
Yet, when had she ever offended a Great Grandmaster to the point of having him come to intercept her in the dead of night, and how had her whereabouts been exposed?
Lu Tianxiang surmised that this individual was not an official Great Grandmaster of Da Qian; otherwise, there would be someone else arriving knowing her whereabouts.
Although the individual posed some threat to her, their realm was at best similar to hers; capturing or subduing her was far from their reach.
She, Lu Tianxiang, the celebrated Mother Wusheng, had survived till now despite being hunted by one at the third level and another at the fourth level of the Myriad Phenomena Realm.
“Who are you, sir? Why do you block my path?”
As her thoughts flowed, Lu Tianxiang spoke out, her tone cold and filled with hostility.
She did not know when she had offended this Great Grandmaster, but she still needed to capture Han Li. Having her route blocked by this person was truly vexing.
Han Li was exceedingly cautious. She had only been searching for Qiu Xuan, and yet, like a startled bird, he was ready to move his household and leave
Yuanzhou.
If he discovered someone was probing for information about him, he could quite possibly abandon his family and concubines, fleeing alone—in which case, she might not be able to find Han Li again.
Da Qian was vast, and she was the wanted Mother Wusheng. She couldn’t openly look for people. Whatever she did was twice the effort for half the result. If Han Li ran to hide in the Capital City of Da Qian, then she could lose all hope.
“And who might you be?”
A robust voice resonated within the Spirit Realm they had constructed with their Spiritual Sense, allowing them to communicate freely without fear of affecting the outside world.
“I will only say this once, stand aside for me!”
Lu Tianxiang’s eyes were filled with murderous intent, her dignified and luxurious face revealing the severity of her threat, giving even Han Li a moment of alarm.
This Great Grandmaster, coming from who knows where, seemed intent on pursuing his migrating group. Han Li had merely wished to obstruct her path and make her retreat. He hadn’t anticipated her swift turn to murderous intent.
Han Li had already observed the woman carefully. She appeared to possess only the cultivation of the Hollow Void Stage, but in actuality, she was a Great Grandmaster of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, her stage slightly higher than his, yet their combat abilities should be similar.
His Divine Spirit and Spiritual Sense were much stronger than Lu Tianxiang’s. She could not see through him, but he could see through the strength she concealed.
He did not wish to do battle with a Great Grandmaster, as it could lead to injuries and reduce his strength. He still needed to protect the migrating group and deal with many crises. He had to maintain peak condition; he would rather have the Great Grandmaster back down.
But if the Great Grandmaster refused to heed reason and insisted on proceeding forward, Han Li would not be courteous. Who would win or lose would only be known after the fight.
He had the Body-Cultivating Furnace in his hand, and by consuming high-grade spirit liquid, he could swiftly repair his injuries and engage in attrition battles. Even if wounded, he could recover to his peak condition in a short time. The only downside was the considerable consumption of the high-grade spirit liquid accumulated in the Body-Cultivating Furnace.
This was his trump card, one he wouldn’t use lightly.
All thoughts flashed through his mind in an instant, and Han Li did not speak. Instead, he prepared in silence. Seeing that Lu Tianxiang was growing impatient, he made his move directly.
Roar!
A dragon’s roar resounded between heaven and earth, shaking all directions, as if to dispel the endless night and return the world to a bright cosmos.
One moment Han Li’s figure vanished from the mountaintop, and the next, he reappeared above Lu Tianxiang. He raised his hand and struck with a palm. A colossal dragon, composed of a vast amount of Gang Yuan blended with the true essence of martial arts, roared toward Lu Tianxiang with killing intent.
When Han Li made a move, he struck with all his power.
As Lu Tianxiang spoke, Han Li had already released the embryonic form of his all-encompassing martial arts true essence. Then, he activated his Vajra Invulnerability protective technique, causing his strength to surge. He still had two hours of invulnerability left under the Vajra state.
With the enhancement from his all-encompassing martial arts, the power of the Vajra Invulnerability protective technique increased significantly, nearly rivaling an Earth-grade superior martial art. Furthermore, Han Li had mastered this technique to perfection, making its power even more formidable.
The Dragon Suppressing Palm was likewise. Enhanced by his all-encompassing martial arts and the divine power of the Vajra Invulnerability technique, its power was almost comparable to an Earth-grade supreme martial art.
This palm strike, delivered from a high position, had astonishing power and immediately left Lu Tianxiang dazed.
She hastily defended, but failed to block it completely, only dissipating about fifty to sixty percent of its power. The remaining force slammed into her delicate body.
Lu Tianxiang was sent flying far away before she could stabilize her figure, blood oozing from the corner of her mouth, her complexion unsightly, with a murderous look covering her beautiful face. This man has no respect for martial arts ethics!
She was careless and did not dodge!
She also did not want to battle with a Great Grandmaster, as it would expose her identity and attract Da Qian’s pursuit. Especially since Prince Wu’an was particularly furious lately, Lu Tianxiang did not want him personally hunting her down, because then she would undoubtedly be doomed.
Her intention was to intimidate the man, to scare him off so that she could continue on her way.
She hadn’t expected him to attack without a word, dealing a blow that caused her to spit blood profusely. It was utterly detestable.
If she hadn’t defended hastily, that palm strike would have inflicted severe injuries and greatly reduced her strength. Even so, she was still lightly wounded.
As her thoughts flowed, Lu Tianxiang also made her move; there was no room for hesitation at this moment.
She brought her palms together, then separated them, and instantly, star fire bloomed around her. Each flame, shaped like a white lotus, was dazzling, illuminating the night.
Each flame contained her martial arts true essence and was a part of an Earth-grade supreme technique that she had nearly perfected.
With a soft cry from Lu Tianxiang, the sky filled with star fire surged toward Han Li in the sky above. Each flame was powerful enough to extinguish a Grandmaster in the initial stage of the Hollow Void Realm, and now there were thousands, even tens of thousands, of them.
Lu Tianxiang was confident that even a Great Grandmaster would suffer immensely if struck by this attack and would sustain severe injuries.
But in the next instant, her expression changed. Han Li struck with another palm, a ferocious dragon roared forth, crushing countless star flames.
Even though Lu Tianxiang dodged in time, she was still grazed by the residual force, causing much of her clothing to be torn, revealing large areas of her fair skin, which was especially conspicuous in the dark night.
She looked toward Han Li, only to see that the remaining star fire that bombarded him was ground to nothing by the protective qi wall surrounding him.

chapters.title: Chapter 105: The Aggrieved Demoness 1
chapters.content:
Chapter 105: The Aggrieved Demoness 1
Translator: 549690339
“Seeking death! ”
Lu Tianxiang was furious. She raised her hand and struck with her palm—a massive palm imprint sweeping across, carrying the intent of a vacuum, to crush everything.
The individual clearly had a lower combat ability than hers, but because they took the initiative and caught her off guard, she now found herself at a disadvantage, having sustained serious injuries. Even her clothes were torn, which added to Lu Tianxiang’s frustration.
After striking with her palm, Lu Tianxiang’s figure vanished from the spot and reappeared behind Han Li, her finger pointing towards the back of Han Li’s head.
This finger contained immense power, in perfect harmony with her martial dao’s true meaning, capable of obliterating all things and destroying all signs of life. If Han Li were to be struck, he would either die or be gravely injured.
Han Li remained silent. As Lu Tianxiang struck with her palm, his palms moved together, one utilizing “Glimpse of the Dragon in the Field” to transform into an indestructible wall of Qi, with mighty dragons rolling upon it, their roars echoing for miles.
At the same time, his right arm bent inward, and his right palm drew a circle, pushing outward with a whoosh, a divine dragon surging forth with a lofty dragon’s roar, blasting towards Lu Tianxiang.
Boom!
Terrifying sounds came from the firmament as Lu Tianxiang and Han Li engaged in a fierce collision, causing a great commotion.
Lu Tianxiang’s palm strike was blocked by the left palm of Han Li, unable to break through the rolling dragon wall. Han Li’s palm strike also missed Lu Tianxiang, her figure had disappeared by then, leaving only the mountain behind her shattered.
When Lu Tianxiang pointed her finger, a smile appeared on Han Li’s face. He did not turn around or take any defensive action; he simply released a palm strike.
This palm strike was supremely firm and resolutely yang, unmatched in sturdiness.
Roar-
The sound of the dragon’s roar reverberated through Leizhou and Qingzhou. Lu Tianxiang was forced to take the full brunt of Han Li’s palm strike head-on, sent flying backward. The front of her clothes shattered completely, leaving a large palm imprint barely missing her chest.
“Cough cough-”
At this moment, Lu Tianxiang was in severe discomfort. Her eyes, filled with disbelief as she looked at Han Li, revealed an attack that was less than impressive, but a defense that was perversely strong.
She had thought that Han Li, without any defense, would succumb to her finger strike, potentially costing him his life. To her surprise, it was not so.
Her finger did possess extreme power, even piercing through Han Li’s protective Qi, but when it touched the back of his head, it felt as though she was pressing against a piece of Immortal Gold—it couldn’t penetrate at all.
Who knows what Han Li’s skull was made of; it was incredibly hard, causing her finger to hurt tremendously. Despite taking her strike, Han Li acted as if nothing had happened.
In contrast, what about her? She was now somewhat battered and bruised.
Although that finger strike did break through Han Li’s protective Qi, a significant portion of the force rebounded back onto her, leaving a small red dot on her forehead as blood seeped out continuously.
She had also borne the brunt of Han Li’s palm strike. As she clashed directly with it, she was nearly pierced through by that single strike, and now she suffered severe injuries.
“Who exactly are you? Are you sure you haven’t mistaken me for someone else?”
Lu Tianxiang watched Han Li warily, taking her medication while she questioned him. Her strength had significantly decreased; unless she resorted to burning her Faith Halo using a secret technique, she had no confidence in defeating Han Li.
She felt utterly cursed, accosted without reason by a Great Grandmaster, beaten into serious injury, and not even knowing who was behind it.
After exchanging several moves with Han Li, she realized he had only used two martial skills, a palm technique and a protective divine ability, neither of which she had ever seen or heard of.
Even the martial dao’s true meaning he exercised was unfamiliar to her. Neither in Daqian nor the Xuan Domain did such a Great Grandmaster exist.
Any Great Grandmaster who had made an appearance would be recorded; anyone who had taken action would have information spread about them.
There were only so many renowned Grandmasters in the Xuan Domain, and none matched this person.
She had never heard of him. They had no shared past grievances or recent disputes, and yet she was waylaid and nearly killed, which left only one possibility: he had mistaken her for someone else.
She must have been mistaken for someone else, and that’s why she was ruthlessly beaten by this Great Grandmaster.
Lu Tianxiang expressed that she felt very aggrieved.
She didn’t want to take the blame for others, nor did she want to fight this person again; most importantly, she simply couldn’t beat him—he was too resilient.
During the fight, this person was like an overbearing tank, with an absurdly high defense and tremendous strength. Every palm strike that landed on her made her cry out in pain.
Her attacks on him, however, were like scratching an itch—they hardly hurt him at all, sometimes not even breaking through his protective aura. Even if it broke, it didn’t cause harm, and she had to bear the tremendous backlash.
In the fight against this person, she could only take hits. Fortunately, her speed was incredibly fast, which allowed her to dodge, or else a few more palm strikes would have killed her.
It was unbearable.
At this moment, the voice of Han Li came, startling the brainstorming Lu Tianxiang.
“Vacuum Palm Imprint, Lifeless Finger, and the White Lotus Secret Method, it turns out you are the Lifeless Mother.”
Looking at Lu Tianxiang from dozens of miles away, Han Li didn’t make another move. Just through the simple exchanges, he had already figured out Lu Tianxiang’s capabilities.
The Lifeless Mother was wanted by the Daqian Empire, with her information made public, practicing nameless cultivation techniques, skilled in martial arts like the Vacuum Palm Imprint, with formidable strength—Han Li had looked at it long ago.
At first, when he saw the Galaxy Fire Lotus, he had his suspicions. After observing the Vacuum Palm Imprint and Lifeless Finger, he confirmed her identity.
He didn’t know why the Lifeless Mother was pursuing his moving convoy, nor would he easily let go of the Lifeless Mother, but the subsequent matters were not for him to worry about anymore.
He needed to leave, and the rest would be handled by the Daqian Empire.
Although Han Li had fought a great battle here against the Lifeless Mother, he never revealed his identity from beginning to end—no one knew that this mysterious Great Grandmaster who had injured the Lifeless Mother was him.
Not waiting for the Lifeless Mother to respond, Han Li sneered coldly, and his figure disappeared from sight.
The Lifeless Mother’s pupils contracted sharply as Han Li surprised her once again. She found that in terms of speed, this person was faster than she was, vanishing from her Spiritual Sense’s coverage area in the blink of an eye, with no trace of his whereabouts.
“Damn it, this is troublesome.”
The Lifeless Mother glanced towards Huozhou, then towards Qingzhou, muttered resentfully, and disappeared from sight.
This accidental grand battle was massive, although not as much as the one in Jizhou, and it attracted the attention of countless powerhouses from Leizhou, Qingzhou, Huozhou, and even the Yinyang Sect.
After all, this was a battle of Great Grandmasters, causing mountains to crumble and the earth to split, affecting a wide area. In Huozhou Province City, two Great Grandmasters were deployed right away and rushed to the battlefield.
Lu Tianxiang ingested and refined a medicinal pill, barely suppressing her injuries and raising her aura a bit. She no longer dared to pursue the ancestor who acquired the Rebirth Pill Formula.
The urgent matter was to escape the pursuit of the Qian Dynasty. It wasn’t too late to settle the score with Han Li afterwards; Lu Tianxiang directly blamed Han Li for the incident.
This time the trouble was all due to him—if not for the ancestor wanting to move house, she would not have pursued him here, only to be blocked and severely roughed up by a mysterious Great Grandmaster.
Lu Tianxiang kept a pent-up frustration in her heart with nowhere to vent. She knew she would be pursued for a while, and with bad luck, she might meet her demise.
This made her even more resentful towards the ancestor-seeking consort Han Li. Wasn’t it good to stay put in Lingjun City? Weren’t you always confined to Lingjun City, never venturing out? What were you wandering around for?
‘l’ne battle ot Great Grandmasters, came as SWIttlY as It went—trom Han Ll suddenly making a move to Lu Tianxiang’s departure, it had only been three or four breaths in duration.
When Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong, two Great Grandmasters, arrived, Lu Tianxiang had already been gone for three breaths.
The two glanced at the battlefield, then in the direction where Han Li had left, and chased after the direction Lu Tianxiang had fled.

chapters.title: Chapter 106 - 106 Mysterious 1
chapters.content:
Chapter 106: Mysterious 1
Translator: 549690339
Huozhou, Province City.
As soon as the great battle in Leizhou occurred, Prince Wu’an was alerted. With just a glance. rage began to burn within him.
How long had it been since the battle in Jizhou, where he slaughtered three grandmasters of the Myriad Phenomena Realm? Not even a year had passed, and now another grandmasters’ battle had erupted in Leizhou.
After his bloody campaign in Jizhou, he had secured a period of peace for the Daqian Empire, a peace now shattered right under his watchful eye.
Officially, Prince Wu’an’s task in Sanzhou was to guard the region and eradicate the remnants of the White Lotus Cult. Leizhou, Qingzhou, and Huozhou were all within his jurisdiction.
It was outright disrespect, time and again challenging him, pulling at his whiskers, akin to seeking death with a lantern in hand as one enters the privy.
What fueled his fury was that one of the parties in the battle of Leizhou was none other than the Sect Hierarch of the White Lotus Cult.
The White Lotus Secret Method, the Vacuum Palm Imprint, the Lifeless Finger… He was intimately aware of these signature skills of the Lifeless Matriarch.
To wait for an opportunity to arise, he had once spared the Lifeless Matriarch, content as long as she didn’t stir trouble before his eyes. But now she had emerged once more to wreak havoc, seemingly tired of living.
Both grandmasters involved in the battle were just at the early stage of the Myriad Phenomena Realm. Aside from his pride preventing him from bullying the weak, a more crucial reason was his reluctance to step foot in Leizhou lightly.
The Prophet of the Imperial Astronomer had recently informed him that his opportunity would be found in Leizhou. Knowing it was there, he felt even more strongly that he must not go to Leizhou.
He had to remain in Huozhou to attract attention, to make those who coveted the opportunity believe it was in Huozhou. Then, when the time was right, he would procure it quietly, and afterwards, no longer need to consider others.
Therefore, he did not move personally but sent Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong to capture and kill the Lifeless Matriarch.
“If you fail to capture and kill the Lifeless Matriarch this time, you know the consequences. ”
The indifferent words of Prince Wu’an made both grandmasters shudder. They hurriedly made their way to the battlefield in Leizhou, hoping that as the two grandmasters continued to fight, the Lifeless Matriarch would have no escape.
After the two grandmasters departed, Prince Wu’an said to the man in blue robes, “Sir Blue, please go as well.”
“Investigate the identity of the other grandmaster. If possible, recruit him. If not, then let it be.”
“Understood.”
Sir Blue nodded slightly, his figure vanishing from sight.
Leizhou battlefield,
The figure in blue stood firm in the sky as his spiritual sense swarmed out, enveloping the entire battlefield, investigating repeatedly.
He had also watched the battle from afar and was quite familiar with the fight between Han Li and Lu Tianxiang. So he played back various scenes in his mind, which eventually took shape.
The scenes started to play, from the moment Han Li struck fiercely, to their intense clash, to Lu Tianxiang’s failed sneak attack that resulted in her serious injury, and finally their separate departures.
These replayed scenes were astonishingly similar to what actually transpired, truly startling.
“This grandly yang and forceful palm technique, the strikingly yang protective divine skill, and that exceptionally fast movement skill…” Sir Blue frowned deeply.
He knew of similar palm techniques and divine skills, but none were identical to the martial skills employed by this mysterious grandmaster.
He did not recall any grandmasters proficient in such fierce martial arts among those who had risen to the Myriad Phenomena Realm in the early stage within the Dast twentv vears.
“A grandmaster from the Yinyang Sect? Or is it all a deception?”
Sir Blue gazed in the direction Han Li had escaped, muttering to himself. After some thought, he pursued in that direction.
He did not have high hopes of finding the mysterious grandmaster, but he had to try; otherwise, he could not justify it to Prince Wu’an.
Sir Blue preferred to wait, not believing that the mysterious grandmaster wouldn’t make another move. With enough actions, their identity would eventually be revealed.
Zhending Manor, outside the province checkpoint.
Han Li had rejoined the migrating caravan.
Having gravely injured the Lifeless Matriarch and deliberately exposed her identity, once he sensed grandmasters from the Daqian Empire approaching, Han Li swiftly retreated.
He certainly didn’t want to encounter any other Great Grandmasters, lest he draw a host of troubles upon himself. His power could be exposed, but his identity could not be easily revealed.
The exposure of his power would only make the outside world think there was one more mysterious Great Grandmaster, but should his identity be exposed, that would indeed bring a lot of trouble.
Even being powerful could attract trouble, such as having to take sides, people seeking assistance, or stronger figures probing how one’s strength surged so rapidly…
This time, Han Li had only used three martial arts techniques: a body protection skill and a palm technique, which were relatively obvious, while his footwork had no distinct features that made it easy to recognize.
Fortunately, all the problems had been solved, and his identity had not been exposed.
As long as no Great Grandmasters attacked afterwards, he wouldn’t need to use his body protection skill and the Dragon Suppressing Palm again. Using the Life-taking Sword Scripture in conjunction with the Zhenjun Sword would be enough to handle most troubles.
After calling over Qiu Yueyao, Han Li lay on her soft, delicate body, caressing her while pondering over the issue with the Mother of No Birth.
He bore no grudge against the Mother of No Birth, so why had she attacked his migrating convoy? There must be a reason.
In the outside world, he was only a Cultivator who had just advanced to the
Gangyuan Realm, not very powerful, nor did he possess any notable treasures or resources that would attract the attention of a Great Grandmaster from the Myriad Phenomena Realm.
Few knew that he held the Body-Cultivating Furnace, so it was unlikely the Mother of No Birth knew about this. Thus, the only treasure on him that could attract a Great Grandmaster would be the Pill Formula for the Rebirth Pill.
The Zhenjun Sword, though an Earth-Level Supreme Magical Artifact, could also attract a Great Grandmaster, but he had never revealed it.
“How exactly did the Mother of No Birth find out?” Han Li pondered.
After obtaining the Rebirth Pill Formula, he had never revealed it. It was an ancient pill formula, and it was impossible for others to deduce it from just a few medicinal ingredients.
It was very likely that there was an issue with Qiu Xuan. Qiu Xuan had been dead for twenty or thirty years, but the place where he obtained the Rebirth Pill Formula still existed.
Han Li suspected that the Mother of No Birth had entered that place and thereby obtained a clue, which led to the pursuit all the way to him.
Now that the Mother of No Birth was pursued by two Great Grandmasters, it was very likely she would meet her demise, which meant his trouble was resolved.
Yinyang Sect, Black Tortoise City.
The third Elder looked in the direction of Leizhou, his expression somewhat
surprised. Were the current Great Grandmasters all rushing to their deaths.
He was very powerful and not very far away; he had discovered the fight between Han Li and Lu Tianxiang right from the beginning.
He had watched the entire battle, recognized the identity of the woman in black as the Mother of No Birth, and also saw that she was no match for the mysterious Great Grandmaster.
“This is a provocation to Prince Wu’an. It seems that the Mysterious Forces behind the Mother of No Birth are about to make a big move,” the third Elder murmured.
He thought Lu Tianxiang’s action was influenced by the forces behind her, he had misjudged the situation, but by sheer coincidence, his misjudgment turned out to be correct.
“However, who is that mysterious Great Grandmaster? To defeat the Mother of No Birth in such a short period of time, they must be strong. How can they remain obscure and unknown?”
The third Elder couldn’t figure it out; he had never seen or heard of the Vajra
Invincible Body Protection Skill or Dragon Suppressing Palm used by Han Li.
Although ignorant of Han Li’s identity, the third Elder did know that Leizhou, Qingzhou, and Huozhou were going to be in chaos.
Repeated battles between Great Grandmasters could potentially set off the entire situation, not to mention that behind the scenes, those Mysterious Forces were fanning the flames.
“The sacrifice is not small, though.”
The Mother of No Birth had come out to create chaos again and now, severely wounded by the mysterious Great Grandmaster, Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong would not miss this opportunity. The Mother of No Birth was doomed.
Sacrificing a Great Grandmaster from the Myriad Phenomena Realm to disrupt the situation, the Mysterious Forces were indeed making a costly move, and thinking of the three Great Grandmasters they had already lost, he couldn’t help but feel astonished at their foundation.
The Yinyang Sect at least wouldn’t dare to sacrifice four Great Grandmasters so easily; they only had twenty-eight Great Grandmasters openly.
But this was also good. With the Mysterious Forces leading the charge, the Yinyang Sect could gain an advantage and at least partition a part of the Daqian Empire’s territory.

chapters.title: Chapter 107 - 107 Fengbo Pavilion_l
chapters.content:
Chapter 107 - 107 Fengbo Pavilion_l
Chapter 107: Fengbo Pavilion_l
Translator: 549690339
The Daqian Empire was home to four states in its eastern region, and Jingzhou was one of them.
Within Jingzhou, there were six major sects, five of which were headed by a Hollow Void Stage Guru, while the last was led by a Great Grandmaster of the Myriad Phenomena Realm.
The Guihun Sect was the foremost among Jingzhou’s six major sects. Its Sect Leader, Yuchi Bu, was a man of formidable strength, widely recognized as the number one powerhouse in Jingzhou.
At this moment, within the Guihun Sect, Sect Leader Yuchi Bu was secretly meeting with an envoy.
This envoy alone possessed peak powers of the Myriad Phenomena Realm, which left Yuchi Bu secretly shocked. The background of the Mysterious Forces was unfathomable if an envoy could easily kill him.
“Sect Leader Yuchi, if there’s no issue, then we should establish the alliance right away,” said the envoy clad in blue robes with a calm tone.
Yuchi Bu hesitated a bit. The envoy represented the Mysterious Forces and had already promised him a wealth of benefits. Upon success, they would elevate the Guihun Sect to new heights.
However, Yuchi Bu was somewhat worried about the Daqian Empire. Once he formed the alliance, he would be entirely opposed to the Daqian Empire, leaving no room for sentiment. Should the news leak, the Daqian Empire would certainly annihilate the Guihun Sect immediately, asserting the empire’s authority.
Seeing his indecision, the envoy sighed inwardly, aware that the offered benefits were still not sufficient, and so he played his last card.
“In addition to the conditions we’ve agreed upon, once our endeavor succeeds, the Guihun Sect can select three disciples every hundred years to study under my faction’s tutelage. We will provide enough resources to cultivate an Emperor Wu of the True Martial Realm for the Guihun Sect within five hundred years.”
Yuchi Bu’s heart leaped with excitement, and without hesitation, he immediately said, “It’s a deal!”
The collaboration with the Mysterious Forces had revealed their substantial resources; they were a formidable power with several Emperor Wus of the True Martial Realm, far surpassing the might of the Daqian Empire.
Their reason for partnering with the Guihun Sect was to foster a proxy—a foreign power like theirs could not personally overthrow the Daqian Empire without facing resistance from all the major forces in the Xuan Domain.
The power structure of the Xuan Domain was well-established, and no faction was keen on letting others steal their share of the territory.
With support from the Mysterious Forces, overturning the Daqian Empire became highly plausible. When that time came, the Guihun Sect would reap great benefits and have the opportunity to advance into the True Martial Realm.
Yuchi Bu knew that the Mysterious Forces had approached multiple sects within the Daqian Empire; even if he refused, others would likely agree, and the empire’s days were numbered.
After leaving the Guihun Sect, the envoy headed towards another place, musing over Yuchi Bu’s greedy appearance while sneering inwardly.
Exiting Jingzhou, the envoy arrived in another state and went deep into a mountain range stretching tens of thousands of miles, where a high building stood. It had thirty-six floors, each six meters high.
Above the main door of the first floor hung a plaque inscribed with three characters: Fengbo Pavilion.
The envoy moved past layer upon layer of formations, ignoring the patrolling cultivators, and arrived at the base of Fengbo Pavilion with a hint of wariness.
He was well aware that Fengbo Pavilion was the headquarters established by the Mysterious Forces within the Daqian Empire and that the pavilion itself was a powerful Heaven Rank Artifact.
The envoy entered Fengbo Pavilion and made his way to the thirty-sixth floor, where an old man was gazing out the window at the scenery. The envoy spoke with great respect:
“Master, your orders have been successfully carried out.”
“Hmm.”
The old man responded nonchalantly, as though the matter was of little consequence. Without turning around, he added:
“Little Tianxiang has been causing some trouble in Leizhou. She’s gotten on the wrong side of Prince Wu’an and is now being pursued by Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong. Will you go help her?”
The envoy felt a chill in his heart and hurriedly said, “I will follow your instructions in all matters.”
He could tell that the old man was somewhat angry. Lu Tianxiang had done something foolish to upset Prince Wu’an, which could potentially disrupt their grand scheme.
If she disrupted the plans of their forces, Lu Tianxiang would surely face severe consequences. If the matter was grave enough, she might even be put to death.
Although the envoy was Lu Tianxiang’s uncle and had taken good care of her, he did not dare to take on this task now, as it could have implications for him as well.
“Let’s see if the little Tianxiang girl makes it back alive,” said the old man before dismissing the envoy and saying no more.
The envoy quietly left Fengbo Pavilion, secretly praying that Lu Tianxiang would be able to evade this assassination attempt.
After inquiring about the situation, the envoy sighed and finally understood why the True Martial Realm master was angry.
Leizhou, Zhenyi Manor.
Under the moonlit night, a figure was frantically fleeing, with two others in hot pursuit.
No matter how the figure ahead tried to escape, those two were tightly on his trail, unable to shake them off.
“Two stubborn plasters!” Lu Tianxiang cursed angrily.
After fleeing the battlefield, she continued to escape while desperately consuming medicine. She had to quickly heal her injuries and recover her strength, or else she was doomed.
But her strength had greatly diminished after being injured, and her speed had also decreased. Before long, Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong had caught up with her.
With no other choice, Lu Tianxiang had to fight while running, constantly disrupting the two men in order to buy herself more time.
Her power was originally not a match for either of the two, and with her injuries, she was even less of an opponent. Her disruptions weren’t very effective, and the two men soon caught up to her again.
After escaping for a hundred thousand li, Lu Tianxiang was almost unable to run anymore, her injuries becoming even more serious, thanks to Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong.
Tens of li behind her, Wan Guiyuan and Yang Tianxiong relentlessly chased her, maintaining communication through whispers and occasionally attacking the Mother of No Life, aggravating her wounds.
In their eyes, this operation was practically a sure win. With their strength, they could have already forcibly subdued Lu Tianxiang, but they were somewhat wary of her fighting back desperately and injuring them significantly.
Moreover, they wanted to handle this matter gracefully. Prince Wu’an had given them two options: capture or kill, and they chose to capture.
Bringing the Mother of No Life back alive would certainly earn them far greater merit. Now that the Mother of No Life was almost out of resistance, she was at their mercy.
“Mother of No Life, surrender immediately, and we may still grant you a way to live,” Wan Guiyuan shouted.
“Dream on! Don’t think I’m unaware of your schemes.”
Lu Tianxiang stopped on a vast grassland, touched her chest with one hand, and sneered.
Indeed, she could run no longer, seeing no hope left. Her Gang Yuan was nearly depleted, and her injuries were worsening. If she continued to flee, she would indeed have no power to resist.
She was even less likely to believe Wan Guiyuan’s nonsense. If captured alive, the fate awaiting her was worse than death.
“Demoness, you’ve got no say in this!”
Yang Tianxiong snorted coldly, his terrifying martial intent descended upon Lu
Tianxiang, creating immense pressure on her as if she were bearing two huge mountains on her shoulders.
Wan Guiyuan’s martial intent also descended, suppressing Lu Tianxiang’s martial intent, creating even more advantages for Yang Tianxiong.
“Am I truly going to die here?” Lu Tianxiang, suffering under the martial intent of two Great Grandmasters, became somewhat delirious.
Her past flashed before her eyes like a swift horse passing a gap, leaving Lu Tianxiang deeply saddened. Not long ago, she was full of vigor, seeing a glimmer of rising hope. Was she going to die now?
Six hundred li away, upon a great mountain, a figure stood, quietly observing this scene.
“What a hassle,” Han Li muttered to himself.
Despite his deliberate concealment, none of the three Great Grandmasters had noticed him.
The Mother of No Life was his enemy; he didn’t want to come back, but he had to because she might know that he had the Rebirth Pill.
If he could save her, he would; if not, he would have to act first.
If the Mother of No Life announced the matter before she died, his troubles would escalate. Compared to dealing with the Daqian Empire, Han Li felt dealing with the Mother of No Life was far easier, many times over. After all, the Mother of No Life couldn’t beat him; he would just have to gravely wound her a few more times and see if she dared to trouble him again.
Besides the matter of the Rebirth Pill Formula, Han Li had another reason for coming here.
